Official homepage — Experience life in Mayfair
Few London addresses place you closer to the city's world-famous shopping, dining and cultural scene than No. 5 Maddox Street. From Regent Street and Bond Street to Soho, the West End and Mayfair's renowned restaurants, some of London's most iconic experiences are all within walking distance.
The area also promises a vibrant art scene, including contemporary galleries and exhibitions at the Royal Academy of Arts.

Official homepage — Central London on you doorstep
With Oxford Circus and Bond Street stations nearby, No. 5 Maddox Street offers excellent connections across the capital. Whether commuting to meetings in the financial district, attending a West End performance or exploring London's authentic neighbourhoods, the city is always within easy reach.

Official contact — getting here
BY CAR: No.5 Maddox St. is located on Maddox Street, just off Regent Street, and can be reached from the A40, Bayswater Road from the West and the A41 which leads onto Baker Street in the North. Parking is available in the area, your concierge can assist with booking.
BY AIR: London Heathrow is the city’s main airport and is approx. 45 minutes drive to the hotel. Gatwick is 1 hour 30 minutes away by taxi. London City Airport also serves the city.
BY TRAIN: The following major train stations are 15 minutes away by car: Victoria, Paddington and King’s Cross/St Pancras.
BY LONDON UNDERGROUND: The following tube stations are approx. 5 minutes walking distance: Oxford Circus - Central, Victoria and Bakerloo line, while Bond Street station is serviced by the Central and Jubilee lines.

Official FAQ — How to get to No. 5 Maddox Street from Heathrow Airport?
You can easily reach No. 5 Maddox Street via public transport: take the Elizabeth line from Heathrow (Terminals 2 & 3, 4, or 5) to Bond Street Station, which takes around 35-40 minutes. From Bond Street, its a short taxi ride, or 10-15 minute walk to Maddox Street.
Alternatively, you can take a taxi or private transfer service directly from Heathrow Airport, which takes around 45 minutes, depending on traffic.

Official FAQ — How far is No.5 Maddox Street from London’s top attractions?
No.5 Maddox Street is located in the heart of Mayfair, one of central London’s most prestigious neighbourhoods. Its prime position offers an exclusive London living experience with exceptional access to the rest of the city.
Maddox Street is just steps from London’s most iconic shopping destinations, including Regent Street, Oxford Circus, and Bond Street. Regent’s Park is approximately a 15-minute stroll away, where you’ll find The London Zoo, the Open-Air Theatre, and more attractions to enjoy.
Attractions such as Buckingham Palace, The British Museum, The London Eye are around 20 minutes via tube or taxi, while the Tower of London, Tate Modern and Tate Britian are around 30 minutes away by tube or taxi.

Official FAQ — What are the nearby attractions, shops, and restaurants close to No.5 Maddox Street?
Situated next to Regent Street, you’re just moments away from London’s luxury boutiques and high-end retailers, department stores, and award-winning restaurants. Some of London’s most well-regarded art galleries are close by, including Hauser & Wirth, Gagosian, and Sadie Coles.
Soho and London’s West End is only a 10–15-minute walk away, famous for its leading theatre-productions and vibrant bar scene. Our neighbourhood guide includes all the local favourites on where best to eat, drink and experience close by.

Official FAQ — What services are included at 56 Welbeck Street luxury serviced apartments?
56 Welbeck Street offers luxury accommodation for those seeking the comfort, privacy, and freedom of an apartment with the added convenience of a hotel. Core services include regular housekeeping, a 24-hour concierge, and custom welcome provisions on arrival.
Guests also benefit from services designed to help you integrate seamlessly into London life, including access to private GPs and premium healthcare, as well as exclusive member rates at the Third Space local health clubs.
Enjoy refined London living and hassle-free stays with all utility bills included within your monthly stay rate.

Official FAQ — What amenities are included at 56 Welbeck Street luxury serviced apartments?
Our apartments are comprised of open plan living spaces with a dining area and kitchen, along with a separate bedroom and bathroom, each tastefully furnished to reflect the regency townhouse style and fully equipped for ease during both short and extended stays. Amenities include:
Fully equipped kitchens and living areas

Private GP access

Official FAQ — How far is 56 Welbeck Street from London’s top attractions?
Situated in Central London, Marylebone serves as a prime homebase with impeccable access to the city. London’s top attractions including Buckingham Palace, The British Museum, Big Ben, the London Eye can typically be reached within 15-20 minutes by public transport.
Additional attractions include Tate Modern, Tate Britain, Portobello Market, and The Tower of London, all of which typically take around 20-35 minutes to get to.
Marylebone offers easy access to London’s pristine Regents Park, which is just a 10-15-minute stroll from 56 Welbeck Street. Its vast green landscape is accessible to all and home to the London Zoo, beautiful rose gardens, a boating lake and more. You’ll also find Primrose Hill located just north of Regents Park.

Official FAQ — What are the closest transport links?
There is an abundance of transport links close to 56 Harley Street; the closest tube stations include:
Regents Park (Bakerloo Line) – Approx 5-minute walk
Great Portland Street (Circle, Hammersmith & City, and Metropolitan Lines) – Approx 7-minute walk
Baker Street (Bakerloo, Jubilee, Circle, Hammersmith & City, and Metropolitan Lines) – Approx 10-minute walk
Bond Street (Central and Jubilee) – Approx 10-minute walk
Oxford Circus Tube – (Central, Bakerloo, Victoria) - Approx 10-minute walk
There’s an array of nearby bus routes which offer easy access to various London locations, including Hamstead Heath, Trafalgar Square, Kings Cross, Paddington and more.
(The “56 Harley Street” wording is printed on this official FAQ as retrieved 2026-08-16.)

Official FAQ — How to get to 56 Welbeck Street from Heathrow Airport?
One of the easiest ways is to take the Elizabeth line from Heathrow Terminals 2 & 3, 4, or 5 to Bond Street Station, which take approximately 30 to 40 minutes. From Bond Street you can continue with a short taxi ride, bus ride, or walk to Welbeck Street depending on luggage or preferences.

Official FAQ — What are the nearby attractions, shops, and restaurants close to 56 Welbeck Street?
Marylebone is loved for its central London location whilst still pertaining its unique character and charming village like feel. It’s home to many must-visit pubs, bars and restaurants, and has a fantastic selection of boutique shops.
It is home to the the UK’s oldest music school Royal Academy of Music, and Wigmore Hall, a music hall for chamber music and intimate classical performances, both of which are within a short walking distance from 56 Welbeck Street.
Another nearby attraction includes The Wallace Collection, which offers fascinating insight into the Marquesses of Hertford and Sir Richard Wallace through a display of 18th-century French paintings, furniture, porcelain, and armoury.
Marylebone neighbours London’s major shopping district - Oxford Circus, Regents Street and Bond Street – the most iconic place in London for high street shopping. It’s also exceptionally close to Mayfair, Soho, London’s West End, and Regents Park, offering endless opportunities for family days out, date nights, and local exploration.
Our neighbourhood guide offers a curated selection of local attractions, restaurants, and bars to help you fully immerse yourself in Marylebone life.

Official FAQ — How close is 56 Welbeck Street to Harley Street?
The Living Rooms London portfolio includes several residences, all within walking distance to Harley Street. 56 Welbeck Street is just a 6-minute walk away from the Harley Street’s most established clinics, offering convenient luxury apartment accommodation for extended stays during treatment and recovery.
Enjoy services built for ultimate convenience, including regular housing, a dedicated concierge, and additional access to private GP and healthcare services. If you require lift access, we recommend viewing our residence at 65 Harley Street.

Official FAQ — Do you welcome guests for medical stays?
Yes, our residences are conveniently located near London's leading healthcare providers, including One Welbeck, The Mayo Clinic, HCA Healthcare, Moorfields Eye Hospital, and more. Enjoy services designed to make your stay as comfortable as possible, including regular housekeeping, support with deliveries, 24-hour concierge, along with a full suite of in-apartment amenities.

Official contact — getting here
BY CAR: 56 Welbeck St. is located on Welbeck Street, close to Wigmore Street and Harley Street, and can be reached from the A40, Bayswater Road from the West and the A41 which leads onto Baker Street in the North. Parking is available in the area, your concierge can assist with booking.
BY AIR: London Heathrow is the city’s main airport and is approx. 45 minutes drive to 56 Welbeck St. Gatwick is 1 hour 30 minutes away by taxi. London City Airport also serves the city.
BY TRAIN: The following major train stations are 15 minutes away by car: Paddington, Victoria and King’s Cross/St Pancras, while Marylebone train station is within 5 minutes by taxi.
BY LONDON UNDERGROUND: The following Tube stations are approx. 5 minutes walking distance: Bond Street - Central and Jubilee lines, while Oxford Circus is serviced by the Central, Victoria and Bakerloo lines.

Official homepage — For stays of every length
Whatever brings you to the city - a project, relocation, extended stay or simply more time to explore London - Weymouth Mews offers a home-from-home experience with flexible lengths of stay and accommodation tailored to your needs. For longer stays, our team can personalise your apartment setup, helping you settle in from the moment you arrive.

Official homepage — Design-led living
Restored by award-winning architects Morrow + Lorraine, Weymouth Mews blends British heritage with contemporary design.
Original architectural features sit alongside carefully curated mid-century furnishings, creating spaces that feel both characterful and understated. Many apartments extend beyond their interiors, with private courtyards, balconies and planted terraces that bring a sense of calm to city living. Every detail has been considered to create spaces that are as comfortable as they are beautiful.

Official homepage — Experience life in Marylebone
Long favoured by writers, designers, entrepreneurs and those seeking a more considered pace of London life, Marylebone combines village-like charm with Central London convenience. Start your morning with coffee from a local café, browse independent boutiques along Marylebone High Street or spend an afternoon exploring nearby Regent's Park. The West End, Soho and Fitzrovia are all within walking distance, while Oxford Street's flagship stores sit just moments away.
Our concierge team is always on hand to share favourite neighbourhood recommendations, helping you experience London more like a local than a visitor.

Official homepage — In the heart of central London
Perfectly positioned between Regent's Park, Oxford Circus and Baker Street, Weymouth Mews offers easy access to every corner of London. For business travellers, Mayfair, Soho, the City and Canary Wharf are all within convenient reach. For leisure guests, some of London's most iconic cultural landmarks, shopping districts and green spaces are just a short walk or tube journey away.
Whether you're commuting to meetings, attending a theatre performance or exploring a new neighbourhood, London is always within easy reach.

Official FAQ — What services are included at Weymouth Mews luxury serviced apartments?
Guests at Weymouth Mews enjoy a unique combination of peaceful mews living and the vibrant buzz of Marylebone High Street, just moments away. Experience hassle-free renting with all utilities and high-speed Wi-Fi included in the rate, along with services such as regular housekeeping, a complimentary welcome provision on arrival, and a dedicated concierge to assist with any request.
We offer seamless integration into local life with access to Third Space Health Clubs as well as private GP and healthcare services, along with additional in-residence services such as dry cleaning and laundry, and access to home entertainment services.

Official FAQ — How far is Weymouth Mews from London’s top attractions?
As one of central London’s most charming neighbourhoods, Marylebone’s prime location offers unparalleled access to the rest of the city. Just a short stroll away from Weymouth Mews is Regent’s Park, home to the London Zoo, an Open-Air Theatre, a boating lake, and beautiful gardens to explore.
Iconic landmarks such as Buckingham Palace, The London Eye, and the Tower of London are all reachable within 20–30 minutes by public transport, while major museums including The British Museum, Tate modern and Tate Britain are also within a similar travel time. For something closer to home, the Wallace Collection is just a 10-minute walk away.

Official FAQ — What Transport Links are close to Weymouth Mews?
Weymouth Mews have several nearby transport links, all within a 5–15-minute walk away. Stations include:
Great Portland Street (Circle, Hammersmith & City, and Metropolitan Lines)
Baker Street (Jubilee Lines)
Regents Park (Bakerloo Line)
Bond Street (Central, Elizabeth, and Jubilee Lines)
Marylebone Railway Station is approximately a 5-minute taxi ride away, offering access to Wembley Stadium, Bicester Village, and Oxford. If you’re travelling from Heathrow Airport, simply take the Elizabeth Line directly to Bond Street, which an approximately 10-15 walk away from Weymouth Mews.

Official FAQ — How can I get to from Heathrow Airport to Weymouth Mews?
You can reach Weymouth Mews easily via public transport. The simplest route is to take the Elizabeth line from Heathrow Terminals 2 & 3, 4, or 5 to Bond Street Station. From there, it’s approximately a 10-minute walk or a short taxi ride to Weymouth Mews.
Alternatively, you can take a taxi or private transfer directly from Heathrow Airport, which typically takes 45–60 minutes, depending on traffic.

Official FAQ — What are the nearby attractions, shops, and restaurants close to Weymouth Mews?
Explore the charm of Marylebone right on your doorstep. This unique neighbourhood offers a village-like feel in the heart of central London and is home to an abundance of independent boutiques, coffee shops, bars, and restaurants.
Just a short stroll away are London’s most iconic shopping destinations, including Oxford Circus, Bond Street, and Regent Street, while neighbouring Mayfair offers luxury boutiques, exclusive bars, and fine dining restaurants. Nearby districts also include Soho, the West End, Fitzrovia, and Regent’s Park.
Our neighbourhood guide includes all the local favourites on where best to eat, drink, and explore close by.

Official FAQ — How close is Weymouth Mews to Harley Street?
Living Rooms London offer a luxury collection of residences in Marylebone, all within walking distance to Harley Street. Weymouth Mews is excellently positioned from Harley Street’s renowned clinics, situated just a five-minute stroll away.
Each apartment at Weymouth Mews offers an idyllic location for rest and recovery during your London visit. Enjoy spacious layouts equipped with all necessary amenities, private outdoor spaces, as well as regular housekeeping services, designed to ensure your stay is relaxed and comfortable.
If you require lift access, we recommend our 65 Harley Street residence.

Official FAQ — Do you welcome guests for medical stays?
Yes, our residences are conveniently located near London's healthcare hub and close to leading healthcare providers, including One Welbeck, The Mayo Clinic, HCA Healthcare, and Moorfields Eye Hospital. Enjoy services designed to make your stay seamless and comfortable, including 24-hour concierge, regular housekeeping, delivery support, and a full list of in-apartment amenities.

The neighbourhood also has a dynamic art and cultural scene with contemporary art galleries, historic museums and music venues as well as easy access to London’s iconic green spaces, including Regent’s Park and Hyde Park. Official FAQ — How far is 74-78 Marylebone Lane from London’s top attractions?
Based in central London, 74-78 Marylebone Lane is exceptionally well located with incredible access to the rest of the city. Regent’s Park is within 10-minute walking distance, where you’ll find the London Zoo, the Open-Air Theatre, a boating lake, café’s and rose filled gardens to enjoy.
Attractions such as The British Museum, Buckingham Palace, and The London Eye can all be reached in 15-20 minutes via public transport, while the Tower of London, Tate modern and Tate Britain, are around 20-30 minutes away by tube or taxi.

Official FAQ — How close is 74-78 Marylebone Lane from Heathrow Airport?
74-78 Marylebone Lane is approximately 35 to 60 minutes from Heathrow Airport, depending on travel method, route, and time of day. If using public transport, take the Elizabeth Line from Heathrow Terminals 2 & 3, Terminal 4, or Terminal 5 directly to Bond Street.
A taxi from Heathrow to Marylebone takes around 40 to 60 minutes depending on traffic.

Official FAQ — What are the nearby attractions, shops, and restaurants within walking distance of Marylebone Lane?
74–78 Marylebone Lane is situated in the heart of Marylebone Village, a charming and unique neighbourhood nestled within vibrant Central London. It is home to an abundance of independent boutiques, coffee shops, restaurants, and bars, all loved by those in the know. The Old Marylebone Town Hall is within a short walking distance, as is the Royal Academy of Music.
Just outside Marylebone Village is the perfect destination for iconic London shopping. A short stroll brings you to Oxford Circus, Bond Street, and Regent Street for high-street shopping, or into the prestigious Mayfair for luxury boutiques, exclusive bars, and restaurants for fine dining.
Our neighbourhood guide includes all the local favourites on where best to eat, drink, and experience close by.

Official FAQ — How close is 74-78 Marylebone Lane to Harley Street?
We offer a collection of Marylebone residences ideal for private healthcare stays in London, all within walking distance from Harley Street. 74-78 Marylebone Lane offers a peaceful and convenient retreat just a six-minute walk from Harley Street’s most renowned clinics.
Our apartments offer bright and modern interiors with premium services designed to ensure a convenient stay, including regular housekeeping, bespoke welcome provisions on arrival, and a dedicated concierge, ensuring a relaxed and comfortable stay for rest and recovery.
If you require lift access, we recommend viewing our residence at 65 Harley Street.

Official FAQ — What are they closest transport links from 74-78 Marylebone Lane?
The closest underground stations are around a 5–10-minute walk away, the nearest being:
Bond Street (Jubilee, Elizabeth, and Central Lines)
Oxford Circus Station (Central, Bakerloo, and Victoria Lines)
Baker Street (Bakerloo, Circle, Hammersmith & City and Metropolitan Lines)
There are several buses stops within a short walking distance from Marylebone Lane, offering easy access to locations across London, including Marble Arch, Hyde Park, Victoria, and Baker Street.
Marylebone Station is a 15-minute walk or short taxi ride from 74–78 Marylebone Lane, which provides access to Wembley stadium, Bicester Village, and Oxford.

Official homepage — For brief visits or extended stays
Whether you're staying for a few nights, several months or somewhere in between, Harley Street offers the flexibility to make London feel like home. Particularly suited to medical stays and longer-term visits, the apartments provide the privacy, comfort and practical support needed for recovery. With lift access to all floors, regular housekeeping, and a dedicated concierge team, we ensure every logistical detail is taken care of.
For extended stays, our team can also tailor your apartment setup, helping you to settle in from the moment you arrive.

Official homepage — Thoughtfully designed interiors
Set within an impressive architectural building originally designed by Claude Ferrier, the property was carefully restored by Barbara Weiss Architects, before undergoing its interior transformation led by London-based studio Waldo Works.
The interiors were designed to complement the building’s original features, while creating a living space that reflects Marylebone’s charming, elegant character. This is achieved with a warm colour palette, contemporary furniture and artwork curated by Laura Bartlett.

Official homepage — Experience Marylebone like a local
Harley Street has long been associated with wellbeing, healthcare and professional excellence, while remaining firmly connected to the wider character of Marylebone. Independent cafés, restaurants, boutiques and green spaces sit alongside some of London's most respected medical institutions, creating a neighbourhood that feels both wellness-focused and welcoming.

Official homepage — Perfectly positioned for London living
Marylebone's Harley Street is within walking distance of Bond Street and Oxford Circus, providing excellent access across London. Whether travelling to appointments, commuting to meetings or exploring the capital's most iconic districts, the city is always within easy reach.

The residences prime location near Harley Street clinics, Marylebone High Street, and Regent’s Park offers guests a perfect balance of city life and natural tranquility, with easy access to Soho just minutes away.

Official FAQ — What services are included at 65 Harley Street luxury serviced apartments?
Ideal for those seeking hassle-free living with all bills included, experience the charm of old British Regency living in a meticulously restored Grade II listed apartment building, located in the heart of London’s prestigious Harley Street.
Our luxury serviced apartments combine the comfort of a private home with the convenience of full-service amenities, including regular housekeeping, a dedicated concierge, and personalised welcome provisions upon arrival.
We go beyond standard hospitality to ensure seamless integration into London life, offering access to private GP services and healthcare, as well as exclusive rates at nearby Third Space health clubs. Enjoy access to additional laundry and dry-cleaning services, as well as curated in-house experiences such as private chef hire.

Official FAQ — What amenities are included at 65 Harley Street luxury serviced apartments?
Our luxury apartments are fully furnished, finished to impeccable standards, and equipped with top-of-the-line fittings and Smeg appliances. Amenities include:
Fully equipped kitchens and living areas
Complimentary high-speed Wi-Fi and smart TVs
Lift access to all floors
Regular housekeeping and linen service
Dedicated concierge service
Laundry and dry-cleaning services (additional charge)
Access to private chefs and curated in-apartment experiences
Private GP access

Official FAQ — How far is 65 Harley Street from London’s top attractions?
Marylebone is centrally located with excellent transport links, making it the perfect home base for exploring London’s top attractions.
Iconic landmarks such as Big Ben, Buckingham Palace, The Shard, and Westminster Abbey are within 20-30 minutes awa, whilst attractions such as Camden Market, West End Theatres, The London Eye, Royal Opera House, Covent Garden, and Portobello Market are all reachable within 20-40 minutes via public transport.
For all things art and history, you’ll find the Wallace Collection just a short stroll away, Mayfair’s iconic art galleries nearby, as well as the Natural History Museum, The British museum, Tate modern and Tate Britain around 15-30 minutes away by public transport.

Official FAQ — How to get to 65 Harley Street from Heathrow Airport?
If you’re travelling from Heathrow Airport, simply take the Elizabeth Line from Heathrow Terminals 2 & 3, 4 and 5, which takes you to Bond Street Station in approximately 30 minutes. From here, it's an approximately 10-minute walk.
Alternatively, taxis are readily available from the airport. The trip to 65 Harley Street usually takes around 45-60 minutes, though it may be longer during peak traffic times.

Official FAQ — What transport links are near 65 Harley Street?
Located in Central London, Harley Street is accessible via several underground stations, the nearest including:
Regent’s park (Bakerloo Line) – Approx. 5-minute walk
Oxford Circus (Central, Victoria and Bakerloo lines) – Approx. 10-minute walk
Bond Street (Central, Elizabeth and Jubilee lines) - Approx 10-minute walk
There’s an abundance of bus routes which stop at or near to Harley Street, all of which take you to various locations across London, including Marble arch, Baker Street, Oxford Circus, Paddington, Great Portland Street Station, and more.

Official FAQ — What are the nearby attractions, shops, and restaurants close to 65 Harley Street?
Besides its unprecedented location to London’s most esteemed Harley Street Clinics, 65 Harley Street is just a short stroll from Marylebone High Street and its charming array of independent café’s, restaurants, shops, and boutiques.
For iconic London shopping, take a stroll down Oxford Street, Regents Street, and Bond Street, or take a 10-minute walk into Mayfair for high end luxury spending or fine dining. Neighbouring Marylebone is bustling Soho, as well as London’s West End for world renowned theatre production.
If you’re looking for refined greenery, Regent’s Park is just a 5–10-minute stroll away, offering huge green landscape with rose gardens, café’s, a boating lake, as well as the London Zoo, and Open-Air Theatre.

Official FAQ — Do you welcome guests for medical stays?
Yes, our residences are just moments from Harley Street’s renowned clinics, including One Welbeck, The Mayo Clinic, HCA Healthcare, and Moorfields Eye Hospital, to name just a few. Our apartments offer a refined, comfortable stay ideal for medical visits, with lift access, a 24-hour concierge, twice-weekly housekeeping, grocery delivery support, and a full range of amenities to support your stay during treatment or recovery.

The collection includes two penthouse apartments, including a five-bedroom residence with an expansive furnished rooftop terrace overlooking the surrounding rooftops of Maida Vale. Each apartment also benefits from secure underground parking - a rarity in London.

Official homepage — A home for effortless West London living
Spacious interiors, access to three acres of private landscaped gardens and secure underground parking make Europa House an ideal base for London living.
Whether travelling as a family, relocating to London, staying with a pet or simply seeking a longer-term London base, each apartment combines the comfort of home with the convenience of serviced living.

Official homepage — For stays of every length
Particularly suited to families, relocation guests and longer stays, Europa House offers the flexibility, comfort and space to settle into London life at your own pace. With generous apartment layouts, private outdoor areas and landscaped gardens on your doorstep, it provides a rare sense of calm within the capital.
For extended stays, our concierge team can personalise your apartment setup, introducing workspaces, family-focused bedrooms or even pet-friendly areas.

Official homepage — A grand residential setting
Set within an impressive period building on one of Little Venice's most attractive residential streets, Europa House combines traditional London architecture with the space and flexibility of modern apartment living. Thoughtfully updated interiors create welcoming spaces designed for both short and extended stays.

Official homepage — Discover Little Venice from Europa House
Little Venice is one of London's most charming residential neighbourhoods, known for its picturesque canals, elegant period architecture, green spaces and village-like atmosphere; it stands apart from London’s busier districts while remaining well-connected to Central London.
Beyond the canals, visitors can explore the iconic Abbey Road Studios, stroll through the serene Regent’s Park, or explore the boutique shops and cafés of Maida Vale, all just minutes away.

Official homepage — Europa House location
Just moments from Maida Vale Underground Station, Europa House offers excellent connections across London while retaining the peaceful character of a residential neighbourhood.
Paddington Station, with direct Heathrow access via the Elizabeth Line and Heathrow Express, is also nearby, making Europa House particularly convenient for international visitors and longer stays.

Official FAQ — Which services are included at Europa House luxury serviced apartments?
Living Rooms London are proud to offer a service that blends the comforts of home with luxury hotel-style hospitality. To ensure effortless London stays, guests can receive regular housekeeping, custom welcome provisions on arrival, and a dedicated concierge available to answer queries and apartment-related requests.
Additional offerings include a dry cleaning and laundry service, SOLICE Healthcare and private GP appointment access and access to private chefs and curated in-apartment experiences via Hometainment.

Official FAQ — How far is Europa House from London’s top attractions?
Europa House is located in West London’s serene, canal-side neighbourhood of Little Venice, a peaceful area with excellent access to the city centre. Enjoy the refined regency living of Europa House in a tranquil setting, while being perfectly positioned to explore all that London has to offer.
Europa is located within walking distance of the iconic Abbey Road Studios as well as Lord’s Cricket Ground, the historic home of cricket. A short walk takes you to the nearest Tube station or Bus stop, from where major attractions such as the Hyde Park, Big Ben, Covent Garden, Soho, West End theatres, and the Westminster area are typically reachable within 30 minutes by public transport.

Official FAQ — What transport links are near Europa House?
The closest tube is Warwick Avenue on the Bakerloo Line, which is approximately a 5-minuete walk away. Europa House is a 15-minute walk or 10-minute Tube ride to Paddington Station, which offers the below transport options:
National Rail
Elizabeth Line
London Underground (Bakerloo, Circle, District and Hammersmith and City lines)
A variety of bus routes are just a 3-to-5-minute walk from Europa House, providing convenient access to central London as well as nearby neighbourhoods including Maida Vale, St John’s Wood and Paddington.

Official FAQ — How close is Europa house from Heathrow Airport?
Heathrow Airport is approximately 15 miles or 24 kilometres from Europa House. This typically taking around 45-60 minutes by car or taxi, or approximately 45 to 60 minutes by public transport.
To go via public transport, simply take the Heathrow Express train from terminals 2 & 3 to Paddington, then take the Bakerloo line to Warwick Avenue, which is just a 5-minute walk to Europa House.

Official FAQ — How close is Europa House to St John & St Elizabeth Hospital and Wellington Hospital?
Our luxury serviced apartments are just a short 15-minute walk or drive from both St John & St Elizabeth Hospital and The Wellington Hospital. Located in peaceful Little Venice, Europa House offers a calm and comfortable home-from-home for guests during prolonged hospital stays in London.
Our apartments are designed for refined comfort and convenience, with lift access and spacious layouts throughout. Our dedicated concierge team is always on hand to assist with anything you may need, from arranging transport to managing grocery deliveries.

Official FAQ — How close is Europe House to the American School in London?
Europa House is just a short 15-minute walk or drive from the American School in London, making it an ideal choice for families looking to enrol.
Situated in the tranquil, residential neighbourhood of Little Venice, just next to St John’s Wood, Europa House offers serviced apartment living ideal for families. The property features spacious, lateral-layout apartments with up to four bedrooms, along with exclusive access to award-winning, three-acre private gardens, complete with a children’s playground.

Official FAQ — Are there any nearby attractions, shops, and restaurants within walking distance of Europa House?
Europa House is within walking distance of a selection of must-visit canal-side restaurants, cafés, and bars. Charming local bakeries, grocers, florists, butchers, and more are also just a short stroll away.
Our neighbourhood guide showcases the very best places to eat, explore, and enjoy nearby. Additionally, our dedicated concierge is always on hand to provide personalised recommendations.
Less than 30 minutes by public transport will take you some of London’s most iconic shopping destinations, including Bond Street and Regent Street, Westfield (White City), and Notting Hill’s Portobello Market.

Official History title: Dolphin Square | History | Iconic Residential Estate in London

Dolphin Square Through Time
Dolphin Square, located in Pimlico, London, boasts a storied history that reflects both grandeur and intrigue. Completed in 1937, this massive apartment complex quickly became a symbol of luxury and modernity, attracting high-profile residents, including politicians, actors, and spies. During World War II, it housed military personnel and was a hub of wartime activity. The post-war era saw Dolphin Square continue as a prestigious address. Despite periods of change, Dolphin Square has remained an iconic fixture in London's architectural and social landscape, embodying a rich tapestry of historical events and cultural shifts.

1935 - 1937 — Costain completes construction on Dolphin Square
Completed in 1937 by builders Costain on the former site of a government-owned army clothing factory, Dolphin Square is a feat of engineering. It cost £1.5 Million to build and took no fewer than 12 million bricks. Dolphin Square officially launched on 25th November 1936.
Credit for the naming of Dolphin Square can be attributed to an uncle of Sir Albert Costain, Director of the company responsible for the construction and early management of Dolphin Square.
A J Costain, headmaster of a school in Colwyn Bay, was staying with the Costain's in London when he mentioned that his school magazine was called 'The Dolphin'. He suggested Dolphin Court, but the layout of the buildings prompted the Costain's to settle on Dolphin Square.
Continuing the nautical theme, it was decided that each of the thirteen houses should be named after Admirals and other well-known figures from the United Kingdom's distinguished maritime history.

1940 - 1950 — The Effects of the Second World War on Dolphin Square
The residents of Dolphin Square endured an eventful Second World War.
Grenville House hosted General De Gaulle's Free French headquarters.
The car park became an ambulance depot, the gymnasium was transformed into a hospital, and the former bicycle shed was the mortuary.
Air raid shelters were provided beneath Frobisher House. i3 bombs hit the square during the Blitz - the biggest of which fell on Frobisher and went thudding through the top four floors.
In 1940, 19-year-old Archie Hancock joined Dolphin Square as an engineer, working across the estate during one of the most significant periods in its history. More than 70 years later, in 2013, we had the privilege of welcoming Mr Hancock back to Dolphin Square to share his remarkable memories.
During the Second World War, Mr Hancock witnessed several bombs strike the Square. He recalled one bomb crashing through the roof and landing on a piano while it was being played. Remarkably, despite the dramatic impact, nobody was killed. Fortunately, the damage caused by the attacks was relatively limited, and extensive rebuilding was not required.
In January 1942, the Free French Forces established a presence at Dolphin Square. Security was exceptionally tight, with special passes required to access the areas they occupied. General Charles de Gaulle was among the notable figures who visited the Square during this time, although Mr Hancock never had the opportunity to see him in person.
Mr Hancock's memories provide a fascinating first-hand insight into Dolphin Square's wartime history and its role during a pivotal chapter of the 20th century.

1950s & 1960s — The "West End" Era of Dolphin Square
During the 1950s, Dolphin Square became one of London's most prestigious residential addresses and residents enjoyed an exceptional level of service. Shoes could be left outside front doors to be cleaned and uniformed porters, instantly recognisable in pillbox hats and white gloves, provided assistance throughout the estate. The Square's restaurant embodied the glamour of London's West End. Residents dressed in evening wear to dine, dance and socialise, creating an atmosphere of elegance that became synonymous with Dolphin Square during this period.
Dolphin Square also attracted significant investment. Costain sold the estate to a property entrepreneur for £2.25 million, and in 1959 it changed hands again for £3.1 million, reflecting its growing reputation and desirability.
In the early 1960s, Dolphin Square's links to espionage once again captured public attention. John Vassall, an Admiralty clerk living in 807 Hood House, was exposed as a Soviet spy in 1962. While rumours persisted that other intelligence operatives had frequented the Square, Vassall remains its most infamous espionage connection.
By the mid-1960s, Westminster City Council purchased the lease of the Square for £4.5 million and sublet it to the Dolphin Square Trust, which managed the estate as a housing association. This marked the beginning of a new chapter in the Square's history while preserving its standing as one of London's most distinctive residential communities.

1970 - 2006 — Home to Politicians, Public Figures and Royal Connections
During the latter decades of the 20th century, Dolphin Square continued to attract a diverse and influential community of residents. Its proximity to the Houses of Parliament made it a popular home for Members of Parliament, peers and public servants from across the political spectrum.
The Square also welcomed a number of high-profile residents and visitors. Princess Anne lived in Drake House during the 1970s, while Princess Diana is said to have used the renowned Dolphin Square swimming pool.
In the 1980s, the estate's gardens underwent a significant transformation with the creation of the Moroccan Garden, following a design competition. Around the same time, the iconic dolphin fountain, created by sculptor James Butler RA, was commissioned, adding a distinctive feature that remains a focal point of the Square today.

2006 - 2020 — Westbrook and the Introduction of Serviced Apartments
In 2006, Dolphin Square entered a new chapter when Dolphin Square Trust and Westminster City Council agreed the sale of the estate to Westbrook. While remaining sensitive to the building's heritage and character, Westbrook embarked on a programme of investment, refreshing communal areas and apartments to meet the needs of modern residents.
A significant milestone came in April 2006 with the closure of the Dolphin Square Hotel. The former hotel rooms were transformed into contemporary serviced apartments as part of a wider regeneration programme, leading to the launch of Dolphin House and broadening the range of accommodation available within the estate.
Throughout this period, the Shopping Arcade remained an important part of daily life at Dolphin Square. Residents and visitors could access a wide range of convenient services, including a dry cleaners, newsagent, hair salon, greengrocer and travel agency, reinforcing the estate's reputation as a self-contained community.
The Bar & Grill became a popular destination for residents and guests, serving seasonal dishes made with herbs and vegetables grown within the Square's own gardens. For relaxation and wellbeing, residents and the wider community enjoyed the award-winning Moroccan-inspired Spa, which became one of Dolphin Square's most distinctive and celebrated amenities.

2020 - Present — AXA Become the Asset Managers and Launch the Restoration Programme
The start of the new decade brought unprecedented challenges as the COVID-19 pandemic impacted communities around the world. During this period, AXA assumed asset management responsibility for Dolphin Square and launched the most significant investment programme in the estate's recent history, aimed at ensuring it continues to meet the needs of modern residents while safeguarding its future for generations to come.
The ambitious Restoration Programme marked the beginning of a new era for Dolphin Square. Rodney, Duncan and Beatty Houses became the first buildings to be taken offline to undergo comprehensive refurbishment, laying the foundations for the long-term renewal of the estate.
While restoration works progressed, Dolphin Square remained a thriving residential community. New initiatives, including the introduction of a pet-friendly policy, reflected the evolving needs of residents, while a programme of events and activities continued to foster a strong sense of community across the Square.
This period has also seen the launch of the largest lift modernisation programme in Dolphin Square's history, with all 28 lifts across the estate scheduled for replacement. Together, these investments are helping to preserve the character of Dolphin Square while enhancing the resident experience and preparing the estate for its next century.

Official Restoration Programme title: Dolphin Square | Restoration Programme | Estate Restoration & Modernisation

It’s almost 90 years since our first residents called Dolphin Square home. The years, advances in technology and our expectations of sustainable living have culminated in the urgent need to preserve, modernise and restore.

CHALLENGE Updating a classic building with people at its heart
APPROACH Discover more about our approach to the restoration of Dolphin Square
TIMINGS Map our journey – understand key dates and milestones
BENEFITS Find out more about positive changes that will affect you, the Square, and the wider environment

Preservation, Improvement & Restoration
Every apartment will undergo important restoration work at some point over the next seven years – delivered on a house by house basis.

Our Guiding Principles:
Firstly, and critically, we recognise that this is your home.
Behind the language of projects, phases and works - this is your home, and we understand and respect that. Your comfort, wellbeing and happiness are our priority. We’ll listen and where you have questions, concerns or queries, will always endeavour to respond as quickly as we can.
We want to and will engage with you individually.
There’s no ‘one size fits all’ approach. As each phase is launched, every affected resident will be contacted individually by a dedicated team to discuss their own particular situation.
We’ll always respect your legal rights.
There’s no question of us acting in any way other than is set out in the terms of your lease. We’ll always carry out our own responsibilities in a full and proper manner.
We’ll ensure we give appropriate, and the maximum possible notice, before the works are due to start.
We recognise people will need time to adjust and will begin the process of engagement with affected residents at the earliest possible opportunity.

Guided by Our Vision for the Restoration Programme
1) To preserve the building.
2) To modernise the mechanical services and the environmental performance of the building.
3) To improve the interiors, amenities and apartments for contemporary living.
4) To protect the gardens, residents and character.
5) To include and value diversity in our community.
6) To restore the attraction of living at this quintessential London address.

Historic Building
Working within a building designed c.90 years ago by architect Gordon Jeeves, Dolphin Square has its own character and sense of place. We’re protecting this through maintaining the fabric of the building – the 125+ tonnes of concrete, 12 million bricks and c.6,000 windows forming its outer walls – and making important improvements to the mechanical services.

Respecting Our Surrounding Environment
...both inside and outside Dolphin Square. We’re proud to be part of the Pimlico Conservation Area. The Restoration Programme will recognise and respect all our neighbours – those who live in and around the estate, as well as the rich flora and fauna that thrive in the listed gardens.

Transforming Dolphin Square
The Restoration Programme is challenged with working at a significant scale, within an established building; we’re driven to embrace and apply new methods and technologies that will achieve the ambitious sustainability targets set for the project. We appreciate that we’ll be the first to face some of these challenges and sharing our research, findings and outputs will benefit the property industry as a whole. Whether insights and learnings into contemporary London living, 1930’s structures or new technologies and innovation, we want to embrace collaboration and sharing, promoting best practice for the benefit of all.

Our Approach
Environmental: Embracing sustainable technologies to reduce energy consumption and carbon emissions.
Social: Creating short- and long-term employment, increasing diversity and inclusion, embracing social enterprises, and creating a special place to live and work in the heart of our Pimlico community.
Governance: Long-term investment ensures responsible and considered stewardship of place and community. Our objective is to preserve all that is valued about Dolphin Square, restoring its reputation as a quintessential London address.
Communication: We know how important it is that we keep everyone informed at every stage of the programme. We’re committed to open, transparent and regular engagement and information sharing.

Hidden Works
Key to the sustainable future of Dolphin Square is investment in its inner workings – the utilities infrastructure, including plumbing, heating and electrical system upgrades. These improvements are designed to enhance the comfort of our residents and secure the long-term future of the estate, whilst addressing some of its more immediate challenges – all dramatically improving the estate’s overall environmental performance.

Interior Canvas - Modern Heritage
The interior design approach takes its inspiration from Dolphin Square’s heritage, with a focus on quality and craftsmanship. The scale of the Restoration Programme creates the opportunity to bring a holistic vision to the entire estate.

Some New Faces Around the Square
The Restoration Programme is assessing every aspect of Dolphin Square to meet the demands and expectations of London living in the 21st century - from the use of space and energy, to the care of our biodiverse environment. To ensure we appropriately and responsibly assess every aspect, our ongoing surveys and inspections span the length and breadth of the entire estate and gardens.

Sustainable Style — in SW1
Dolphin Square has always been an iconic address – the grand scale of its 1930’s vision, home to many from London’s rich and diverse society. The building character and style remain, but internally the mechanical improvements will bring Dolphin Square firmly into the modern age – re-engineered to meet and exceed today’s environmental standards.

A Sustainable Design to Promote the Highest Levels of Comfort & Well-Being
Dolphin Square’s 1,200+ apartments present a combined total of more than 6,000 windows – replacing all of these will be the most significant single factor in reducing energy consumption – heat loss in the winter and heat gain in the summer.

Efficiency Will Improve Performance / Conscientious Living
We’re all becoming more aware of our individual impact on the environment. Our carbon footprint is just one measure. It’s far more sustainable to retain the structure of a building and coupled with our harnessing of new green technology, the Restoration Programme is embracing opportunities and initiatives to improve the overall performance and operational efficiency of Dolphin Square. Together, we’ll reduce energy consumption and waste for the benefit of the environment and our future generations.

Enhanced Amenities & Shared Spaces
The Restoration Programme will create new spaces, both inside and out – flexible areas to enhance the experience of living at Dolphin Square. Health and well-being are such an important part of our everyday, so alongside the restored Fitness Club, swimming pool and spa, there will be additional amenities and services to stimulate mind, body and soul.

Official Restoration team (as printed): Ilaria Ferraboli, Head of Interiors - Grid Inside (GRID Architects) — “We’re going far beyond just redecoration in order to improve the estate for modern living at this quintessential London address.” The improvements can be categorised into four main parts: the apartments and common areas to each house; the amenity spaces; the building envelope; and the basement. Fundamental to our approach is capitalising on the 1930’s character of the exterior building in the new interior design. Laure Ferrand, Associate Director – Longevity Partners — setting a future-proof sustainability strategy, “making it a priority for Dolphin Square to get as close as possible to a net-zero building.” Divya Harirami Herrero, Innovation & Energy Consultant - Longevity Partners — “My key priority is to align the scheme to a future-proof Net Zero Carbon framework such as the RIBA 2030 Climate Change Challenge.” Clodagh Cant, Sustainability & Energy Analyst – Longevity Partners — BREEAM and WELL as the foundation of the sustainability strategy.

Official property page — Things to do around Baker Street Serviced Apartments

Introduction
Smart, thriving and bursting with class, this is a beautiful inner-city location in central London. The whole area holds a brilliant combination of refinement and charm, with a distinctive blend of red brick and white stone townhouses. Bordered by Soho, Mayfair, Fitzrovia, Paddington and The West End; all of which provide the perfect reason to centre yourself in this hub of activity and attraction. While here, step back in time with a visit to the Sherlock Holmes Museum, the official home of the famous fictional detective; enter a world of Victorian curiosities, and explore objects from Sherlock Holmes’ most famous cases. At The Wallace Collection you’ll find an extraordinary assortment of paintings, sculpture, ceramics, and more, housed in a historic townhouse – marvel at masterpieces by artists such as Rembrandt, Rubens and Velázquez, to name a few. Fans of photography should head to Atlas Gallery, which hosts contemporary exhibitions as well as displaying vintage twentieth-century snaps.

Shopping
The area is home to some of the most vibrant shopping streets in London. Glamourous Chiltern Street oozes cool, with a host of independent shops: find premium fashion at Sunspel, a curated selection of clothing, jewellery and gifts from Mouki Mou, and high-quality whiskeys at Cadenhead. One independent shop that is a delight to behold is Daunt Books, housed in a beautiful Edwardian building with long oak galleries and graceful skylights - find it around six minutes’ walk from our apartments in nearby Marylebone. Further afield, the retail mecca of Oxford Street can be reached in around 11 minutes via the Bakerloo Line, while Soho’s pedestrianized shopping spot, Carnaby Street, is around 14 minutes away on the Bakerloo Line. In both of these renowned retail hotspots you’ll find designer stores, high street brands, independent boutiques and more.

Food & Drink
If you want to breakfast with a beverage and a pastry, there’s a branch of Joe & The Juice and a GAIL’s Bakery a couple of minutes away; or visit Buns From Home for hand-rolled croissant buns made fresh throughout the day. Monocle Café, brought to you by Monocle magazine, also offers a great selection of baked goods and drinks in cool surrounds, and 106 Baker Street is a lovely spot to pick up some delicious pastries, cakes and sandwiches to enjoy in your apartment. For lunch and dinner, the options are seemingly endless in this bustling part of town. In the immediate vicinity of our apartments, Kitchen at Holmes is a refined all-day Mediterranean bar and restaurant with a lovely terrace for sunny days, while popular spot Mielo offers upscale Mediterranean tapas. Il Blandford’s is an unassuming little café on nearby Chiltern Street which is a firm local favourite: offering a selection of Italian family recipes in the restaurant, with a separate wine bar and outside terrace space.

Night Life
Two minutes from our apartments you’ll find the Baker Street branch of Everyman Cinema, the boutique picture palace chain showing a range of blockbuster and independent flicks. Or head to the Marylebone Theatre (8 minutes’ walk) which offers a vibrant evening programme spanning theatre from emerging artists, spoken word performances and monthly comedy shows. Afterwards, have a drink in historic surrounds at one of London’s last remaining ‘free houses’; established 1791, The Barley Mow (3 minutes walk) offers a good selection of drinks, with occasional live music and a darts lounge to boot. In the vaulted basement of cellar bar Purl (6 minutes’ walk) you’ll find innovative takes on classic cocktails in speakeasy-style surrounds. Burlock Rum Room (12 minutes’ walk) is a hidden, 1930s-style Havana bar featuring – you guessed it – rum-based cocktails, as well as weekly live reggae.

Official property page — Things to do around Holborn Serviced Apartments

Introduction
Holborn is brimming with history for the curious to explore; it seems you can’t go a few yards without seeing a centuries-old pub, the majestic Royal Courts of Justice are a sight to behold (after all, Holborn is the heart of London’s legal profession) and Sir John Soane's Museum, a six-minute walk from our apartments (and free to visit) houses an incredible collection of antiquities, furniture, sculptures, architectural drawings, and paintings including work by Hogarth, Turner and Canaletto. There are also plenty of modern delights for visitors of all ages - Harry Potter fans should join the famous boy wizard tour that passes many of the film's various locations throughout London, including King's Cross Station, 12 Grimmauld Place and the Leaky Cauldron. Ever heard of boutique bowling? After visiting the All Star Lanes in Holborn, you'll understand the meaning! Classed as an 'ultimate escape', this American-styled bowling venue is a great place to meet, eat, drink and bowl in style. Or head to Bounce, a cocktail bar and pizza restaurant with 17 ping pong tables to keep you occupied!

Shopping
Holborn is well-placed for a retail fix! Jewellery shoppers will love to browse Hatton Garden’s diamond boutiques – while there, head to Leather Lane Market, a foodie’s paradise. A 15-minute walk will get you to the delights of Neal’s Yard in nearby Covent Garden; this colourful courtyard is not only incredibly pretty on camera, but it is jam-packed with shops to explore. High Holborn, formed off the extension off Oxford Street, offers a wide selection of both retail stores and popular restaurant chains. If you are willing to venture further down the road, you'll finally arrive at the UK's most popular shopping destination, Oxford Street, from the Tottenham Court Rd end. There are also some amazing (and unusual) independent shops in the area. Timorous Beasties designs incredible prints for everything from tea towels to lampshades, rugs and furniture; Jarndyce Booksellers is the antique bookshop of your dreams, housed in an 18th-century building opposite the British Museum; and on Lamb’s Conduit Street, Folk offers well-made casual clothing in lush, exclusive fabrics.

Food & Drink
On Red Lion Street you’ll find Kozzy Café, perfect for a beverage, breakfast or brunch. For the best cup of English tea, visit the Twining's flagship shop at the Strand, the oldest tea shop in London! You may like to visit popular Ciao Bella for a classic Italian lunch or dinner in an airy basement, with framed photos and hanging instruments. Bleeding Heart Yard, a 12-minute walk from our apartments, is a cobbled courtyard where you’ll find a vibrant French bistro and terrace, as well as an extensive wine bar on the ground floor of the historic Bleeding Heart Tavern. With medieval roots, Holborn is peppered with historic pubs. 11 minutes’ walk from our apartments is Ye Olde Mitre, tucked away in a small alley. Build in the 1540s, the pub is famous for having a cherry tree that Queen Elizabeth once danced around with Sir Christopher Hatton. Ye Olde Cheshire Cheese on Fleet Street is one of London’s most famous chophouses. Located in the heart of the capital’s publishing district, this drinking den has played host to history’s literary darlings, including Mark Twain, W.B. Yeats and Charles Dickens, who featured it in A Tale of Two Cities!

Night Life
The Garden Cinema, 10 minutes’ walk from our apartments, is an independent joint with a touch of art deco class. With comfy screening rooms, a curated selection of films and a bar, it's a great venue to enjoy your evening. If you prefer live theatre, head towards Drury Lane where you’re spoiled for choice – The Shaftesbury Theatre, the Gillian Lynne Theatre, the Novello, the Theatre Royal Drury Lane, the Lyceum…take your pick! Or catch a performance of world-class opera or ballet at the Royal Opera House. After, you could enjoy a nightcap at one of the many bars in Holborn. Visit Baranis for specialist herb-infused cocktails, absinthe and the UK’s only indoor pétanque court in this unique basement bar around the corner from the Law Society Hall. Like gin? Well you’re in luck, as The Gin Bar has over 500 to choose from, including well-known brands, small-batch suppliers and local distillers.

Our Ibis House serviced apartments are housed within a newly renovated, purpose built block of flats located right in the heart of pretty Richmond.

The nine apartments have been interior designed to a very high standard. These serviced apartments comprise a mixture of one and two bedroom flats, with the two bedrooms having two bathrooms too.

Bedrooms are spacious with either King or Super King beds. All offer a modern bathroom and a fully equipped kitchen/diner.

Using passivhaus principles of design, these London apartments are quiet, comfortable and extremely energy efficient. This accommodation incorporates high levels of insulation, wooden triple-glazed windows and mechanical ventilation with heat recovery. This means that our Richmond apartments enjoy a comfortable and constant temperature, with fresh air regularly circulated throughout. Remote controlled heating and sound systems add to the building’s state-of-the-art yet homely features.

Richmond Ibis House is a 5-7 minute walk from Richmond station, which provides access to the district line and other overground services.

Official property page — Things to do around Richmond Serviced Apartments

Introduction

Richmond is a picturesque upmarket area of West London, steeped in culture and history. With stunning views of the Thames, the expansive plains of Richmond Park, historic royal houses and a high street studded with independent shops, restaurants and swish gastropubs, it’s easy to see why visitors flock here. Our centrally-located apartments are in easy reach of renowned attractions in the area. Take a pleasant stroll to Richmond Park to photograph the deer, or enjoy the botanical wonders of Kew Gardens. If you're a fan of historic architecture, you’re in luck: Hampton Court Palace (Henry VIII’s royal home), Marble Hill House and Ham House & Garden are all found in Richmond. The area also offers great arts venues: the Landmark Arts Centre offers an eclectic programme of music, comedy and annual arts fairs, while the Richmond Theatre is a popular choice for drama, comedy and children’s theatre. Another nearby destination is none other than Twickenham Stadium, a world-famous venue that is home to the England rugby team.

Shopping

Richmond is certainly not short of places to shop, with a great mix of local suppliers, popular retailers and department stores on George Street and The Quadrant. Try Margaret Howell for contemporary designer fashion, L’Occitane for natural beauty, family-owned India Jane for refined homeware, or The Source Bulk Foods for plastic-free bulk food and household products. On the weekend, take a 10-minute stroll to Duck Pond Market, which hosts stalls from the best local crafters, artists, food producers and ethical businesses. Pick up some gourmet delights to enjoy back at your apartment, and enjoy the live music as you browse. Keep an eye out - famous faces have been known to attend too!

Food & Drink

Well-known for its fantastic cafés, pubs and restaurants, Richmond has a vibrant and varied gastronomical scene. For a great breakfast and coffee, cosy Café Nano is just two minutes from our apartments. Or head down Worple Way to The Alberts Deli, an award-winning independent coffee shop serving breakfast, brunch and lunch options. There are also amazing places by the river that offer a warm welcome and great food and drink with a view. Peggy Jean at Riverside Green offers Australian-style brunches on a restored barge, Scott’s delivers exceptional seafood with a delightful waterfront terrace, and Stein’s brings you Bavarian dishes and German beers overlooking the Thames. The restaurant at Petersham Nurseries is quite unlike others: enjoy a seasonal menu under a canopy of fragrant blooms in this greenhouse restaurant, which has been awarded a Michelin Green Star to recognise its commitment to sustainability.

Night Life

A show at the Richmond Theatre is a great way to kick-start your evening; it’s been a part of the Richmond community since 1899, offering quality drama, musicals, opera, and dance. If you’re interested in live music, The Mitre is a charming pub in a 19th-century building just 8 minutes’ walk from our apartments, with musicians playing every Sunday. The Richmond Vault also has live music as well as great cocktails and beers, and lots of cosy nooks in which to enjoy a drink with friends. For bars, there are plenty of choices within 10 minutes’ walk of our apartments. Dropkick Jonny’s is a secret whiskey and cocktail saloon housed in the attic at Tap Tavern while So Bar serves upmarket drinks in a sleek and intimate venue, as well as tapas. The vibrant botanical-themed interiors of Rock and Rose form a glamorous backdrop for the delicious cocktails on offer. No1a Duke Street, nestled near Richmond Green, is a neighbourhood staple offering contemporary surrounds, curated playlists and a great selection of drinks.

Official property page — Things to do around West Finchley Serviced Apartments

Introduction
West Finchley is a residential area in Barnet popular with professionals and families seeking a peaceful atmosphere with plenty of green spaces, yet easy commuting into the city via the tube. From our West Finchley apartments, you can get to the glorious greenery of Hampstead Heath in around 13 minutes by car, or 30 minutes by tube. Explore the parkland that inspired both the Chronicles of Narnia and John Constable’s later paintings, and admire the city skyline from Parliament Hill. Nearby Kenwood House is one of London’s hidden gems – this mansion house on the edge of Hampstead Heath features a stunning art collection, including pieces by Vermeer, Rembrandt, Gainsborough, Turner and Constable, gorgeous gardens and beautiful interiors to marvel at. Fun can also be found at Finchley's Great North Leisure Park, which houses a lido, Vue multiplex cinema and bowling. Also nearby is Finchley Golf Club, a picturesque 18-hole parkland course just 13 minutes’ walk from our apartments.

Shopping
Brent Cross Shopping Centre can be reached in less than 30 minutes; here you will find 120+ fashion, technology, jewellery, books and homeware stores, from high street heroes to curated smaller labels. Anthropologie houses boho-chic womenswear and home décor; Space NK collates niche and under-the-radar beauty brands; Kiehl’s offers luxury skincare as well as treatments; and Russell & Bromley sells upscale footwear. For designer brands and large flagship stores, head to London’s most popular shopping destination, Oxford Street – just 30 minutes away by tube.

Food & Drink
There are a number of food and drink options in a short walking distance. Tintico’s Finchley location is a great spot for specialty ethically-sourced coffee and delicious pastries near Finchley Central station (13 minute walk). The House (12 minute walk) is a lovely Italian restaurant with rustic décor and a menu of classic pastas and pizzas, as well as weekend brunch. For sushi and Japanese dishes, try neighbourhood restaurant Taro (13 minute walk). On Regents Park Road, Vynam is an intimate dining room with a relaxed vibe and a menu of traditional Vietnamese dishes while Uncle Tony’s Taverna (13 minute walk) is a popular place serving traditional Greek food, with a convivial atmosphere and smart blue-and-white décor that brings a touch of Santorini to North London.

Night Life
Head to the characterful King of Prussia pub (13 minute walk) on Regents Park Road for a rotating selection of craft beer, cocktails and regular events. There’s also a shuffleboard and jukebox which you can enjoy free of charge, making for a fun evening. A little further down the road is The Catcher in the Rye (15 minute walk), a local pub that has been serving up great food and drink to the Finchley community since 1994. Official property page — Things to do around Victoria Serviced Apartments - Westrovia

Introduction
Conveniently located near Pimlico underground station, our Westrovia serviced apartments are close to many of London’s most renowned landmarks and attractions. Buckingham Palace is around 20 minutes’ walk away, and nearby St James’s Park is great for a stroll – this Grade I listed royal park is known for its pelicans, which were originally gifted to Charles II in 1664! Alternatively, take a pleasant 7-minute walk from our apartments down to the riverfront, where you can stroll along Millbank with its excellent views of the Thames. On the way, stop in at the Tate Britain to explore 500 years of British art, from the pre-Raphaelites and JMW Turner to David Hockney and more. Then continue along the river until you reach the iconic landmarks of Big Ben, Westminster Abbey and the Houses of Parliament. Across Westminster Bridge you’ll find the towering London Eye and The London Aquarium, as well as the Southbank Centre, Europe’s largest centre for the arts. It comprises three performance venues and the Hayward Gallery, and is great for both children and adults alike.

Shopping
The Victoria Place shopping centre, located inside the station, contains a variety of health and beauty, fashion and homeware stores, while Cardinal Place is a covered retail development near Westminster Cathedral. Inside you can shop high street brands or take a breather at one of the restaurants, and it also has a roof garden to enjoy on sunny days – there’s seating and Wi-Fi which makes it a lovely spot for an al-fresco lunch. London’s famous Oxford Street can be reached in about 10 minutes from our apartments via the London Underground from Pimlico – here you’ll find high street heroes alongside premium brands and designers. For boutiques, head to the famous Sloane Square shopping district, just one tube line stop from Victoria Station.

Food & Drink
For breakfast or brunch, there are a few lovely options near our apartments. Tachbrook Bakery, Patisserie and Coffee Shop is a family-run neighbourhood spot, while The Roasting specialises in Italian espresso drinks and café eats. Or head to the Regency Café (6 minute walk from our apartments); opened in 1946, you might recognise this art-deco styled eatery from films such as Layer Cake, Brighton Rock and Rocketman! Make a stop at Market Halls Victoria (13 minute walk) where you can discover a diverse range of food vendors spread across three floors including Asian cuisine, tacos, burgers and more. For a fine dining experience, Muse by Tom Aikens (about 24 minutes from our apartments) offers a special menu from the Michelin-starred chef in an intimate mews house hosting just 25 covers. Other great options for dinner include Iberia, serving traditional Georgian dishes, or Lorne, a creative British restaurant with an elevated wine list – both are less than 10 minutes’ walk from our apartments.

Night Life
Kick off your evening with a show and head towards Victoria station where you’ll find two West End theatres – the Victoria Palace Theatre directly opposite the front of the station and the Victoria Apollo Theatre, home to longstanding hit musical Wicked, around the side. Darts fans might want to check out trendy Flight Club Victoria to try their hand at the arrows. Westrovia has plenty of great pubs tucked away, from upscale gastropubs to historic boozers. CASK Pub & Kitchen, 3 minutes from our apartments, is the epitome of a ‘local’ – set up in 2009 by Pimlico resident Martin Hayes, this award-winning pub combines great food and world-class beers with weekly live music and a convivial atmosphere. The Marquis of Westminster (7 minute walk) offers sophisticated drinks and a menu of high-quality pub classics, while the Queens Arms has been serving pints to the people of Pimlico since 1846.

These wonderful serviced apartments are set right in the heart of busy central London, opposite the lovely Vincent Square, a large grass-covered playing field owned by the nearby Westminster School.

Each apartment has been decorated to a very high standard and includes a well-equipped kitchen with a dishwasher and washer/dryer. The open-plan living area of each serviced apartment features a practical dining table, comfortable sofa / lounging area and a 42 inch smart TV. Bedrooms are furnished with comfort in mind and plenty of storage space. Bathrooms are sleek and modern.

The immediate surrounding area offers a multitude of shopping and dining choices and Victoria station is a mere 1/2 mile / 10 minutes walk away for opportunities across the capital.

Official property page — Things to do around Victoria Serviced Apartments - Vincent Square/Bloomburg Street

Introduction
Our apartments are located on a lovely tree-lined street, yet with the major transport hub that is Victoria Station just a 10 minute walk away and many of London’s most renowned landmarks and attractions in easy reach. Buckingham Palace is around 17 minutes’ walk away, where you can explore the State Rooms on certain dates and see the regular Changing the Guard ceremony. A pleasant 10-minute walk from our apartments will get you to the riverfront, where you can stroll along Millbank with its excellent views of the Thames before you reach the iconic landmarks of Big Ben, Westminster Abbey and the Houses of Parliament. Stop in at the Tate Britain to explore 500 years of British art, from the pre-Raphaelites and JMW Turner to David Hockney and more. Across Westminster Bridge you’ll find the towering London Eye and The London Aquarium. As well as the riverside walking paths, you can enjoy a stroll at St James’s Park, only 15 minutes’ walk away; spot the pelicans as you wander through this Grade I listed royal park - the water birds have been a famous feature here since a Russian ambassador donated them to Charles II in 1664.

Shopping
The Victoria Place shopping centre, located inside the station, contains a variety of health and beauty, fashion and homeware stores, while Cardinal Place is a covered retail development nearby. Inside you can shop high street brands or take a breather at one of the restaurants, and it also has a roof garden to enjoy on sunny days – there’s seating and Wi-Fi which makes it a lovely spot for an al-fresco lunch. London’s famous Oxford Street can be reached in about 14 minutes from our apartments via the London Underground from Victoria Station – here you’ll find high street heroes alongside premium brands and designers. For boutiques, head to the famous Sloane Square shopping district, just one tube line stop from Victoria Station.

Food & Drink
Popular art deco-styled Regency Café is just 2 minutes’ walk from our apartments, making it a great spot for a coffee and breakfast. Opened in 1946, you might recognise this no-frills eatery from films such as Layer Cake, Brighton Rock and Rocketman! For lunch, head to Market Halls Victoria where you’ll be spoiled for choice with a diverse range of food vendors spread across three floors, all housed in a gorgeous Edwardian building. Thai, tacos, Asian cuisine, burgers and so much more are on offer. And if you’re here later in the day on a Thursday or Saturday, you can also enjoy a DJ set while you supper! For dinner, find fine Italian dishes at Santini and cured Spanish flavours at Iberica, both of which offer outside space for a spot of al-fresco dining. Or for something truly special, head to Muse by Tom Aikens(about 20 minutes from our apartments); here you can experience fine dining from the Michelin-starred chef in an intimate and exclusive mews house hosting just 25 covers.

Night Life
With two West End theatres less than ten minutes’ walk from our apartments, you can kick start your evening with a show. Find the Victoria Palace Theatre directly opposite the front of the station and the Victoria Apollo Theatre, home to longstanding hit musical Wicked, around the side. Darts fans might want to head to trendy Flight Club Victoria to try their hand at the arrows. Or enjoy a beverage at one of the quirky bars scattered around Victoria: the impressive whisky bar at Boisdale brings you the best of the Highlands in the heart of London while Clarendon Cocktail Cellar(secreted beneath Artist Residence London) has a menu of cult movie-inspired cocktails. And for a cosy tucked-away pub with lashings of history, stop in at the Cask and Glass, just around the corner from Buckingham Palace.

Official property page — Things to do around Queen's Park Serviced Apartments

Introduction
Queen’s Park is packed with Victorian and Edwardian houses clustered around the eponymous 12-hectare park, where you’ll find beautiful flower gardens, tennis courts, a golf course, bandstand, playground and paddling pool. Salusbury Road is undoubtedly the area’s community hub, offering a range of independent shops, cafés and eateries to explore. With excellent transport links, you’re well situated to get across the capital: Queen’s Park station is a four-minute walk away, with trains to Euston and Paddington, and the chic neighbourhoods of Kensal Rise, Notting Hill and West Hampstead are all easily accessible. Heathrow is a 45-minute drive away via the M4. The Regent’s Park is only 20 minutes from your serviced apartment, where you can hire a rowing boat, enjoy the abundant greenery, visit the open-air theatre or London Zoo. Primrose Hill is an excellent spot to take in the iconic London skyline.

Shopping
There is a plethora of high street and independent brands along and around Salusbury Road, ranging from organic grocery shops to artisan cafés and esteemed eateries. The family-friendly weekly farmer’s market takes place just opposite Viridian Apartments, offering free range and organic produce as well as items sold by artisans. Bookworms should check out family-owned Queen’s Park Books, carrying classic and contemporary reads; it is also the partner of the annual Queen’s Park Book Festival. Further down the street, Ediit carries a range of women’s fashion brands, such as Fabienne Chapot, M.A.B.E., and Samsoe + Samsoe. Towards Kensal Rise, you’ll find plenty of boutique fashion, homeware and gifting stores on hip Chamberlayne Road. And iconic Portobello Road Market is only 25 minutes from your serviced apartment, with stalls selling antiques, bric-a-brac, fashion and more – the perfect spot for treasure hunters. Although the market is open every day of the week, on Saturdays you’ll find all its vendors are in full swing; the energy, colour and hustle is inescapable.

Food & Drink
Salusbury Road offers an array of gastropubs and independent restaurants just a few moments’ walk away. Dark Habit, right next door to your apartment, is the place to go for seasonal, single origin, speciality coffee. For meals out, chic eatery Milk Beach offers all-day dining options, from brunch and sharing plates to mouth-watering mains; all inspired by the diverse cultures that make up modern Australian cuisine. Sushi fans need look no further than Michiko Sushino, where you’ll find traditional yet modern Japanese dishes in a relaxed atmosphere. And at Carmel, you can enjoy delicious Eastern Mediterranean dishes throughout the day as it has a sizeable brunch, lunch and dinner menu. If you want to put your kitchen to good use while staying with us there is a Sainsbury’s, Marks and Spencer, and Planet Organic all in walking distance from your apartment.

Night Life
There are some lovely bars and pubs in close walking distance. Wolfpack is a popular local spot to meet with friends and colleagues for a relaxed evening - the industrial-chic bar offers eight rotating taps of the freshest local craft beer as well as a wine selection, and everyone is welcome! The Salusbury Pub has been under the same management for 20 years and is a real community gem: with pavement tables, it’s a great place to enjoy a sunny evening. Kensal Rise’s iconic Chamberlayne Road is just a 20-minute walk away and will provide even more variety when it comes to cool bars and lovely pubs. While you’re here, stop in at the Lexi, London’s only social enterprise cinema. The independent picture palace is run by volunteers and shows everything from mainstream films to live opera, with proceeds going to charity.
