Official property page — Things to do around Marylebone Serviced Apartments - Chiltern Street

Introduction
Our stylish serviced apartments are just a 5-minute walk from Baker Street Station and a 5-minute walk to fashionable Marylebone High Street. They are ideally situated for access to the cafés, bistros, designer shops and art galleries which characterise beautiful Marylebone Village. The beautiful expanses of The Regent’s Park are just a 10-minute walk away, where you can enjoy the open-air theatre, walk through rose gardens, or boat around the lake. Here you will also find London Zoo, which makes for a great day out for all the family. The theatre haven of London’s West End can be reached in around 20 minutes by public transport, where you will be spoiled for choice when it comes to comedy, drama, musicals and children’s theatre. Fans of art should visit the Wallace Collection, just six minutes from our apartments, which houses an astonishing array of paintings, sculpture, furniture and more in a historic London town house.

Shopping
Marylebone Village offers a unique blend of independent shops and larger, high-street brands. High quality products and attention to personal service is the prevailing norm. Down Chiltern Street itself you’ll find fashion designer Bella Freud, stylish men’s tailoring store Trunk Clothiers Ltd. and health and beauty shop, anatome, among so many others. A few streets away, Marylebone High Street is peppered with premium boutiques, designers, and upmarket perfumeries – while there, do stop in at the beautiful Edwardian bookshop, Daunt Books, to enjoy the stunning architecture while you browse for your next read. The varied shopping areas of Bond Street and Oxford Street, are also within easy walking distance, where you’ll find big-name brands, flagship stores, suave tailoring and more.

Food & Drink
From famous headline restaurants to sweet, vegan inspired cafés, Marylebone is heaven for food lovers, whatever your taste or fancy. Chiltern Street and the immediate roads around it boast so many great choices for breakfast, lunch or dinner – mere moments from your apartment. Arro London is a lovely spot to pick up organic coffee, Italian pastries, sandwiches and more. Or head to Chiltern Street Deli, where you can purchase artisanal produce to use in your apartment kitchen as well as coffee, sandwiches and homemade treats. For dinner, check out the Italian cuisine on offer at rustic Anacapri and Il Blandfords, or head to Chotto Matte, which serves a Japanese-Peruvian fusion menu in a vibrant, modern space. Mielo, meanwhile, is a lovely spot for modern Mediterranean and delicious drinks.

Night Life
Take the tube from Baker Street down to London’s West End, where you’ll find a multitude of theatres showing evening performances of drama, comedy, musicals, cabaret and more. The Top Secret Comedy Club is an unassuming basement venue around the corner from The Shaftesbury Theatre where you can see up and coming comedians and (occasionally!) a big name trying out new material. The Barley Mow is a traditional independent pub, offering historic surroundings in which to enjoy an evening drink, while The Marylebone is a modern bar specializing in fun, creative cocktails. For a really interesting place to have a drink, head to the brick-lined 19th-century cellar bar at Purl London, where they serve intricate, multi-sensory cocktails in speakeasy-style surroundings.

Official property page — Things to do around Marylebone Serviced Apartments - Gloucester Place

Introduction
With Marylebone mainline station and Marylebone and Baker Street underground stations all a 5-minute walk away, these apartments offer superb transport networks throughout London and beyond. Meanwhile London City Airport is 11 miles away, and can be reached with the convenience of public transport. Gloucester Place is a short stroll from the Regents Park, where you can enjoy an open-air theatre, walk through rose gardens, or boat around the lake – or take a 20-minute stroll to the green expanses of Hyde Park. The Sherlock Holmes Museum, a 3-minute walk away on nearby Baker Street, is the official home of the famous fictional detective – step back in time to explore curios from some of Holmes’ most famous cases. Madame Tussauds, home to 150 celebrity figures, is around 7 minutes’ walk away. The Marylebone Theatre is a new performance space offering a programme of theatre, concerts and dance – but you can also reach London’s West End theatres within around 25 minutes via the tube. The world-renowned Harley Street, with its large number of private specialists in medicine and surgery is also a short walk away.

Shopping
Marylebone Village is bursting with a great mix of independent suppliers and high street retailers. The vibrant high street is around 13 minutes’ walk from Gloucester Place; head to Diptyque for luxury perfume, Fabriano Boutique for high-end stationery, Agnes B for chic designer clothing combining French aesthetics with a contemporary edge, or stop in at The White Company for stylish homeware and lifestyle items. The high street is also perfect for fashionistas looking for something unique, as it’s peppered with boutiques such as Fursac for sharp menswear, as well as recognisable womenswear labels including Sandro, RIXO, ba&sh, Bimba y Lola and more. The eclectic shopping areas of Oxford Street and Bond Street are only a few stops away on the tube, where you can find designer shops, department stores such as Selfridges, and a number of upmarket boutiques.

Food & Drink
Marylebone is awash with amazing places to eat and drink. Near our Gloucester Place apartments you’ll find plenty of spots to enjoy your morning coffee, a laid-back lunch or something fancier for supper. Paris’s Café & Restaurant (3 min walk) offers a great selection of sandwiches, cakes and afternoon tea, while the Dorset Café (2 min walk) is a quaint spot serving brasserie-style food – both perfect for breakfast, lunch or brunch. Reubens (9 min walk) is the UK’s longest-running kosher restaurant and deli – it’s the place to go for salt beef sandwiches, latkes, schnitzel and more, perfect for a takeaway lunch. For dinner, try Ali Baba Restaurant, a cosy family-run place serving Egyptian cuisine just a minute from our apartments. Or you could head to one of the nearby gastropubs for a classic British pub supper – the Sir John Balcombe (3 min walk) was the site of the first Lord’s cricket ground and now serves delicious food in a bright, split-level building. For an upmarket evening meal, try Les 110 de Taillevant on Cavendish Street, with a French menu and over a hundred wines available by the glass to pair.

Night Life
Hop on the tube down to London’s West End, where you’ll find a plenty of theatres showing evening performances of drama, comedy, musicals, cabaret and more – there’s something to suit all tastes! Wigmore Hall is the place for prestigious chamber music concerts, or head to 229 The Venue for gigs from contemporary artists as well as club nights. Or perhaps spend your evening at one of the many bars in Marylebone. Burlock Rum Room is a 1930s-style basement bar with vintage touches to the surroundings, while those who prefer wine might want to check out Clarette for its extensive list of French vintages and chic art deco décor.

Official property page — Things to do around Marylebone Serviced Apartments - Crawford Street

Introduction
In the heart of the West End, Marylebone Village is a highly sought-after residential area, nestled between Bond Street, Regents Park, Harley Street and Oxford Street. The beautiful expanses of The Regent’s Park are just a 10-minute walk away, where you can enjoy the open-air theatre, walk through rose gardens, or boat around the lake. Here you will also find London Zoo, which makes for a great day out for all the family. Hyde Park is also found around 15 minutes’ walk away, where you can enjoy the green spaces, take in artwork at the Serpentine Gallery or visit Kensington Palace and the beautiful gardens that surround it. London’s West End theatres can be reached in around 20 minutes by public transport, offering a range of comedy, drama, musicals and children’s plays to enjoy. Fans of art should visit the Wallace Collection, which houses an astonishing array of paintings, sculpture, furniture and more in a historic London town house.

Shopping
Marylebone Village offers a unique blend of independent shops and larger, high-street brands. High quality products and attention to personal service is the prevailing norm. It’s only an 8-minute walk to Marylebone High Street, flanked with fashion, homeware, jewellery, lifestyle and beauty stores. Stop in at Bayley & Sage for artisanal produce to take back to your apartment kitchen; Sezane and Maje for contemporary womenswear; Luca Faloni for timeless menswear classics; or Fresh for luxury skincare. For even more shopping, London’s iconic Oxford Street is around 13 minutes’ walk away, where you’ll find big-name brands, flagship stores, suave tailoring, and department stores such as Selfridges.

Food & Drink
Whether it’s a laid-back brunch, an afternoon coffee and cake or fine-dining you’re looking for, this neighbourhood offers plenty of excellent eateries and bars. Boxcar Baker & Deli is a community spot offering pastries, breads, sandwiches and wraps, as well as coffee – a great place to grab breakfast or lunch. Delamina Kitchen, set up by a wife-and-husband team, serves Middle Eastern dishes in welcoming, informal surroundings. Cavita takes you on a journey through Mexican flavours, colours and traditions – and in the basement you can find Mayahuel Mezcaleria, a secret mezcal bar serving signature cocktails. Twist Connubio, just at the end of Crawford Street, is a popular tapas spot with a wine menu to pair.

Night Life
Take the tube from Marble Arch to London’s West End, where you’ll find a multitude of theatres showing evening performances of drama, comedy, musicals, cabaret and more. If you’re looking to enjoy a relaxed drink and cozy food, The Larrik is a neighbourhood favourite, offering the charm of tradition right in the buzz of central London. There are also plenty of lovely pubs in Marylebone. The Duke of Wellington, just down Crawford Street, has a heated terrace and homely interiors, as well as great choice of food and drink; The Coach Makers Arms, built some 140 years ago, has a classic pub on the ground floor and a hidden 1970s-styled basement bar where you can enjoy a tasty cocktail.

Official property page — Things to do around Chelsea Serviced Apartments - Draycott Place

Introduction
Sloane Square underground station is 8 minutes' walk away, with Kensington, Victoria, Olympia and The City of London an easy tube ride away; some of London’s most iconic attractions, including Stamford Bridge, Hyde Park, Kensington Gardens, Buckingham Palace and the Royal Albert Hall are all less than two miles away and easily reached by public transport. A few moments from our apartments you’ll find iconic King’s Road, boasting a wealth of shopping, bars, eateries and contemporary art exhibitions showcasing the work of emerging artists at the Saatchi Gallery – the artwork is certain to spark lively conversation! There are plenty of lovely side-streets to explore off King’s Road, including colourful Bywater Street which is flanked by townhouses with pastel-painted facades. Take a 13-minute walk towards the riverfront and you’ll discover the Chelsea Physic Garden, one of Britain’s oldest botanical gardens. Across Albert Bridge, you can explore the sprawling acres of greenery at Battersea Park, which has an English garden, pagoda, children’s zoo, boating lake and café where the whole family can while away a sunny afternoon.

Shopping
King’s Road is one of London’s best shopping destinations, with over 160 shops including the iconic Peter Jones department store, independent boutiques and well-known brands. Smaller retailers here include the fantastically creative Bimba y Lola (expect bright colours and seriously playful pieces), British perfume house Penhaligon’s, and Anthropologie, where you’ll find a curated selection of homeware, fashion and beauty from independent brands. Two minutes from our serviced apartments bookworms can get lost in the shelves at John Sandoe Books which are crammed with thousands of fiction, non-fiction and classic titles. For even more retail therapy, Knightsbridge is a pleasant 10-minute stroll away – here you can enjoy the wonderful shopping at Harrods, Harvey Nichols and the delights of designer shops and boutiques.

Food & Drink
This high-end London neighbourhood has a fittingly vibrant bar and restaurant scene, serving up a variety of delicious fare a stone’s throw from our serviced apartments. For fresh organic food all day, head to Daylesford Organic which has a café as well as a farm shop on site; while at Maitre Choux, you can purchase eclairs made by a three Michelin star-experienced chef. The idyllic Ivy Chelsea Garden courtyard is a perfect spot for brunch on a sunny day, while the art-filled interiors are a beautiful backdrop to the modern British menu. For dinner, there are plenty of options: for mouth-watering Indian food in an elegant townhouse, try Kutir, just three minutes’ walk from our apartments. Cinquecento is the place for Neapolitan pizzas and an extensive wine list served up in a cosy, charming space. Head to Dinings SW3 for sushi and cocktails, Ottolenghi Chelsea for Mediterranean-inspired bites or check out 28°-50° Chelsea for delicious European food in chic surrounds, and a curated wine list to pair.

Night Life
Described by the New York Times as "the most important theatre in Europe", the Royal Court is Britain's leading national company dedicated to showing work by innovative new writers – kick off your evening with a show that will no doubt spark lively conversation over drinks afterwards. And there are plenty of unique and quirky bars in the vicinity: Barts is a speakeasy cocktail bar with eccentric wall ornaments and dressing-up boxes (they also do a vintage afternoon tea) while at The Goat pub you can venture upstairs to enjoy cocktails in sultry surrounds. Towards Chelsea Harbour, 606 Club is a highly-rated jazz club and eclectic restaurant with nightly live music from British-based musicians: ingredients for a great night out!

Official property page — Things to do around Chelsea Serviced Apartments - Sloane Avenue

Introduction
Located in the heart of The Royal Borough of Kensington & Chelsea, our apartments are just a few moments from glamourous Sloane Square. At the junction of Sloane Street and King’s Road, Sloane Square is a mecca for shopping fans, while also being flanked by cultural landmarks such as the Royal Court Theatre and Cadogan Hall. Our serviced apartments are well-placed for exploring London’s vibrant art scene, with the Saatchi Gallery just a short walk away at Duke of York Square, and the Tate Britain and the Serpentine Gallery at Hyde Park both easily visited by public transport. While there, be sure to explore the rest of London’s most iconic park, including Kensington Palace and Gardens and boating along the Serpentine. Head down to the riverfront and cross Chelsea Bridge to visit Battersea Power Station, a decommissioned Grade II* listed coal-fired power station, now open as an exciting shopping and leisure destination. You can also buy tickets to ascend 109 metres up the northwest chimney, offering stunning 360-degree views of London’s skyline.

Shopping
The main shopping thoroughfare in this part of the capital is the charming King’s Road, boasting an attractive mix of boutiques and international fashion houses. The excellent amenities of Knightsbridge are within easy reach with famous shopping experiences including Harrods and Harvey Nichols. Smaller retailers here include the fantastically creative Bimba y Lola (expect bright colours and seriously playful pieces), British perfume house Penhaligon’s, and Anthropologie, where you’ll find a curated selection of homeware, fashion and beauty from independent brands. Peter Jones department store, housed in a Grade II* listed building, is just off Sloane Square, offering eight floors of the best in beauty, home, giftware, technology and electrical items.

Food & Drink
Chelsea is a bustling hotspot for an eclectic range of cafés and restaurants. Just off Sloane Square, Colbert offers an all-day Parisian menu taking you from breakfast and coffee through to lunch and dinner. The walls are lined with art and local memorabilia, lending an authentic French bistro feel to this eatery. Bluebird is something of a Chelsea institution, a 15-minute walk from our apartments down bustling King’s Road, with a modern European menu and outside terraces to enjoy on summer evenings. You may also want to try Dinings SW3 for sushi and cocktails, Ottolenghi Chelsea for Mediterranean-inspired bites or 28°-50° Chelsea for delicious European food in chic surrounds, and a curated wine list to pair.

Night Life
Our apartments’ proximity to Sloane Square means you’re not far from a performance venue to kickstart your evening. The Royal Court is Britain's leading national theatre company dedicated to showing work by innovative new writers, while Cadogan Hall is one of London’s best classical music venues and home of the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra – you’ll also find performances from jazz and folk musicians taking place here. Tucked down the immaculately kept residential streets are a number of gastropubs, while those searching for late-night cocktails will be spoilt for choice with swanky bars aplenty. The Botanist, just off Sloane Square, is a firm favourite for its expertly crafted cocktails. A short walk down Sloane Avenue, you’ll find speakeasy cocktail bar Barts, with eccentric wall ornaments and dressing-up boxes (they also do a vintage afternoon tea).

Official property page — Things to do around Marylebone  Serviced Apartments - Miles Place

Introduction
Smart, thriving and bursting with class, this is a beautiful central London location and you’ll find our Miles Place serviced apartments situated right in the heart. The area is bordered by Soho, Camden Town, Mayfair, Fitzrovia, Paddington and The West End; all of which provide the perfect reason to centre yourself in this hub of activity and attraction. Edgeware Road station is a two-minute walk, where you can catch the Bakerloo, Circle, District and Hammersmith & City lines around the capital. Paddington Station is around 13 minutes’ walk away, for onwards travel to the regions. The proximity to Paddington also means you can reach a lesser-known gem of London, Little Venice, in around 15 minutes’ walk. In this charming area, you’ll find quaint waterways and canal-side gardens to explore, as well as a plethora of restaurants and bars. You’re also within easy walking distance of the many cultural attractions of Marylebone, such as the Sherlock Holmes Museum, the Wallace Collection and Madame Tussauds, as well as the lush swathes of Regent’s Park.

Shopping
One of the best parts about the area is its relation to thriving centres of entertainment and shopping, easily reached via the excellent transport links at Edgware Road. Marylebone High Street is around 14 minutes away by tube, peppered with specialist boutiques selling fashion, accessories, homeware, beauty and more. Oxford Street, with its proliferation of designer shops, department stores and upmarket boutiques, can be reached in around 8 minutes via the Bakerloo line while the iconic Portobello Road Market is just 23 minutes away by tube. If you are here on a Sunday, visit the Marylebone Farmer's Market to explore a wide assortment of seasonal foods from artisan producers. There’s always something new, with excellent vegetables, fruit, seafood, meat and poultry sourced from British farms.

Food & Drink
Near our Miles Place apartments you’ll find plenty of spots to enjoy your morning coffee, a laid-back lunch or something for supper. About five minutes’ walk from Miles Place you’ll find coffee shop IRENE, brought to you by a family-owned artisanal bakery – head there for Gentleman Baristas coffees and fresh-baked pastries, perfect for a takeaway breakfast. For lunch, you could try wood-fired pizzas and Italian classics at Zonzo, or check out the mouthwatering delicacies at family-run Vietnamese restaurant Nep Nep. There are also some lovely dinner options alongside the Paddington arm of the Grand Union Canal, about 10-15 minutes walk from our Miles Place apartments, including some great canal-boat restaurants located on the water! The Cheese Barge is a cosy and quirky boat restaurant with an entirely cheese-based menu, plus innovative pairings of small-batch wines. At the family-run floating restaurant London Shell Co, you’ll find a menu of seafood and fish with a curated wine list to match. Meanwhile Bondi Green serves an expansive menu of Australian dishes, in stylish and funky interiors, with a terrace to enjoy the canal-side location on sunny days.

Night Life
Hop on the tube down to London’s West End, where you’ll find a plenty of theatres showing evening performances of drama, comedy, musicals, cabaret and more – there’s something to suit all tastes! Or perhaps try one of the great pubs and bars in the immediate area. Five minutes from our apartments, sophisticated cocktail bar The Perseverance Marylebone offers a speakeasy-style interior with innovative twists on your favourite classics, as well as a delicious selection of non-alcoholic treats too. The bar also hosts weekly live jazz nights. For a casual drink with family, friends or colleagues, try the Sir John Balcombe pub, about 13 minutes’ walk away – it was the site of the first Lord’s cricket ground and now serves delicious food in a bright, split-level building.

Official property page — Things to do around Chelsea Serviced Apartments - West House

Introduction
Chelsea is an affluent area boasting a vibrant gastronomical scene, chic boutiques and gorgeous townhouses. Sloane Square underground station is a short walk away from our apartments, with easy access to Kensington, Victoria, Olympia and the City of London. Some of London’s most iconic attractions can be found within two miles, including Stamford Bridge, Hyde Park, Kensington Gardens, Buckingham Palace and the Royal Albert Hall – all easily reached by public transport. Fans of museums are in luck, with Exhibition Road a pleasant 14-minute walk away; here you’ll find the V&A Museum, the Natural History Museum and the Science Museum – all great options for a family day out! In the nineteenth century, Chelsea was a hub for Victorian artists such as Rossetti, Turner and Whistler – nowadays, find your art fix at the Saatchi Gallery, the Pontone Gallery or Clarendon Fine Arts. If you fancy a stroll, head down to Chelsea embankment for views of the Thames; while there, you may want to visit the hidden gem that is Chelsea Physic Garden, which was established in the 1600s to grow medicinal plants and still houses some 5,000 plants today.

Shopping
Explore fashion, beauty, food and culture in the heart of Chelsea at Duke of York Square, just seven minutes’ walk from our serviced apartments. The Square has over 30 chic boutiques, along with seven restaurants offering al fresco dining. What’s more, every Saturday it hosts an open-air Fine Food Market, curated by Partridges, offering artisanal and locally-produced gourmet foods – stalls include traditional Sicilian desserts at Casa Cannoli, British staple fish ‘n’ chips (with a twist) at Fins & Trotters, and handmade filo pastries at Hush Hush Chefs, among so many others! On King’s Road you’ll find a mile-long stretch of more than 160 shops including the iconic Peter Jones department store, independent boutiques and well-known brands. And with a delightful 10-minute walk, you’ll be in the retail heaven that is Brompton Road in Knightsbridge, where you can explore iconic Harrods, home to big-name brands, independent boutiques and high-end designers selling fashion, accessories, luxury beauty, fine jewellery and watches, food, furniture and more. Knightsbridge is also home to Harvey Nichols and a range of independent designer shops and boutiques.

Food & Drink
Some of the best London eateries can be found in this area. Like to start the day with a caffeine fix? Birley Bakery in nearby Chelsea Green (five minutes’ walk) is styled after a traditional French boulangerie-pâtisserie and serves amazing coffee and sweet treats. While inside, do check out the hand-painted wall murals – a feast for the eyes. The idyllic Ivy Chelsea Garden is the perfect spot for brunch; enjoy modern British menus in a refined, art-filled space or head out to the garden terrace on sunny days. For dinner, neighbourhood favourite Daphne’s is four minutes’ walk away: experience authentic Italian dishes while you admire the European artwork gracing the walls. Another brilliant spot a few moments’ walk from our apartments is 28°-50° Chelsea, a chic restaurant offering a relaxed yet elegant ambience, a seasonal modern European menu and exceptional wine to pair. Or head to nearby Knightsbridge to try British classics in renowned steakhouse Hawksmoor, just 11 minutes’ walk from our apartments.

Night Life
Start the night with a performance at iconic Royal Albert Hall in nearby South Kensington. Since the hall's opening by Queen Victoria in 1871, the world's leading artists have appeared on its stage, and it boasts a varied programme. Or perhaps catch a showing at luxury cinema Fulham Road Picture House – after, you can head to the Hollywood Arms pub to enjoy a drink in beautiful pastel-perfect interiors. For live theatre, look no further than the Royal Court, Britain's leading national company dedicated to showing work by innovative new writers. Inside the theatre, the Samuel French Bookshop hosts live events with playwrights, stocks a range of scripts and drama books, and sells coffee – get there early evening to have a browse before your show. If you want to enjoy a nightcap after an evening of theatre, try the delightful cocktails at Jak’s on Walton Street while you settle into the comfy sofas – and the bar is just a six-minute walk back to our apartments!

Stylish and sleek studio and one-bedroom serviced apartments, nestled within a prime location, right by London Bridge Station.

These apartments have been furnished to a very high standard and include a fully equipped kitchen, air-conditioning and free wi-fi throughout. The bespoke décor and amenities are designed for visual impact and yet have high functionality. Metro wall tiles blend effortlessly with floral feature walls and the exposed brick, white washed panelling and wooden flooring add warmth and character.

The studio within this building offers an open plan living area with a wall-mounted flat screen TV, together with a comfortable sofa and coffee table. The comfy double bed fits conveniently in a cosy corner. Wall and velux windows allow natural light to flood in to the space. The fully-fitted kitchen offers much more than many standard studios with a combi-oven-microwave, hob, washer-dryer, Smeg fridge-freezer, dishwasher, trendy Belfast sink and plenty of cupboard space. The separate shower room echoes the design within the kitchen with Metro tiles and sleek modern fittings.

The three one-bedroom apartments here offer a spacious living area with corner sofas, flat-screen TVs and bar tables for dining. Quality kitchen appliances are as with the studio and large windows maximise the daylight. The double, comfortable bedrooms offer plenty of wardrobe space. The modern, yet practical shower rooms offer a luxurious feel with cleverly-designed lighting. Sofa beds can also be found within all apartments.

Guests will find onward travel very easy - London Bridge underground and train station is a quick 2 minute walk away. Perfect for business or leisure stays - enjoy superb London lifestyle at this serviced apartment from Viridian Apartments, right in the heart of the capital.

Official property page — Things to do around London Bridge Serviced Apartments - 88a Tooley Street

Introduction
Stretching between London Bridge and Tower Bridge, this is one of the capital’s oldest areas. It’s one of the busiest too, with all genres of entertainment found right on your doorstep, including a huge variety of restaurants, bars and numerous cultural landmarks. Get the full Elizabethan era experience by going aboard the Golden Hinde, a 16th-century reconstruction of Sir Francis Drake’s Galleon; or visit Shakespeare’s Globe, a reconstruction of the playhouse for which the renowned bard wrote his plays. While here, explore modern and contemporary art at the Tate Modern, with immersive installations in the iconic Turbine Hall. History buffs will also enjoy a tour of the nine decks of HMS Belfast, a warship that survived World War 2; or head across Tower Bridge to the iconic Tower of London, a World Heritage Site where you can explore the castle and meet the famous ravens that guard the tower. And of course, you can take in the city skyline at the Shard, London’s highest public viewing gallery.

Shopping
The Hays Galleria, a redeveloped wharf, has now become a shopping complex, exuding its history in its glass-roofed walkway. Browse the market stalls for arts and crafts, and souvenirs. Or hop on the Jubilee line and get to London's most popular shopping district around Oxford Street. Foodies should head to famous Borough Market to stock up on amazing produce to enjoy in your apartment, or sample divine food from the many stalls inside this historic building. Borough Market is one of the largest and oldest food markets in the capital and has a long heritage – there’s been a market on the site dating back to the twelfth century!

Food & Drink
For seasonally sourced, single origin coffee, pop across the road to Harris + Hoole. Within a couple of minutes’ walk of your apartment you’ll find a wide range of lunch and dinner options: Plants of Roselyn is the place to go for plant-based authentic Thai cuisine; Flat Iron London Bridge is an industrial-chic steak restaurant; and Pizza Pilgrims is a pizzeria housed in a beautiful archway under London Bridge station, offering outside seating and creative toppings; and Santo Remedio is a Mexican restaurant offering a cool take on traditional street food in gorgeous, bright surrounds. For something special, head to one of the restaurants housed in the Shard, or try the sophisticated South African cuisine on offer at Vivat Bacchus.

Night Life
There are so many bars in the immediate vicinity, you truly are spoiled for choice! Try retro-styled Electric Shuffle for drinks and shuffleboard games under the arches of London Bridge station. At Katzenjammers, lederhosen-clad staff will serve you Bavarian beers at wooden benches while a live oompah band entertains the beer hall. On Holyrood Street, Nine Lives is an amazing snug neighbourhood gem of a cocktail bar, offering brilliant drinks and a great soundtrack in a Victorian basement. And there are, of course, plenty of traditional pubs and taverns – The George, a 17th-century coaching inn, is one of London’s oldest pubs and featured in Charles Dickens’ Little Dorrit. Or for a drink with riverside views, head to the beer garden at The Anchor – it’s the sole survivor of the river taverns of Shakespeare’s day, having been rebuilt after the great fire of London.

Official property page — neighbourhood and apartment
Discover the epitome of urban living at our expansive London Bridge serviced apartments, nestled in the vibrant heart of the city, where every moment pulses with energy, making it an ideal retreat for both business and leisure travellers alike.

Step into the open-plan living spaces of our spacious apartments, boasting a cozy lounging area complete with 42-inch Smart TV. The well-equipped kitchen beckons culinary enthusiasts with its array of modern amenities, including a dishwasher and washer/dryer. Gather around the dining table, perfect for savoring home-cooked meals or doubling as a productive workspace.

Our bedrooms prioritise comfort and restfulness, with quality mattresses, whilst also offering practical storage solutions for your belongings. Our bathrooms are modern and efficient, designed to meet your practical needs.

Tailor your stay to your needs with a choice between our one and two-bedroom apartments, accommodating varying group sizes with ease. For larger families or groups, one two-bedroom apartment offers an additional single bedroom, comfortably accommodating up to five guests.

Elevate your experience in our top-floor apartment, featuring a private balcony spanning the bedrooms, offering a serene outdoor oasis amidst the bustling cityscape. Should privacy outdoors be a priority for you, kindly connect with our reservations team to secure this coveted amenity (stay@viridianapartments.com).

Alternatively, all guests are invited to indulge in the breathtaking vistas from our communal terrace, providing views of the iconic Shard, the crown jewel of London's skyline.

London Bridge underground and train station is 3 minutes walk away, offering onward travel around London and beyond.

Official property page — Things to do around London Bridge Serviced Apartments - 118 Tooley Street

Introduction
Stretching between London Bridge and Tower Bridge, this is one of the capital’s oldest areas. It’s one of the busiest too, with all genres of entertainment found right on your doorstep, including a huge variety of restaurants, bars and numerous cultural landmarks. Get the full Elizabethan era experience by going aboard the Golden Hinde, a 16th-century reconstruction of Sir Francis Drake’s Galleon; or visit Shakespeare’s Globe, a reconstruction of the playhouse for which renowned bard wrote his plays. While here, explore modern and contemporary art at the Tate Modern, with immersive installations in the iconic Turbine Hall. History buffs will also enjoy a tour of the nine decks of HMS Belfast, a warship that survived World War 2; or head across Tower Bridge to the iconic Tower of London, a World Heritage Site where you can explore the castle and meet the famous ravens that guard the tower. And of course, you can take in the city skyline at the Shard, London’s highest public viewing gallery.

Shopping
Once a delivery dock for international shipments, The Hays Galleria - a redeveloped wharf, has now become a shopping complex, exuding its history in its glass-roofed walkway. With a range of permanent stores as well as stalls, you can find everything from children’s designer wear to a refreshingly cool beverage. Take the Jubilee line and get to London's most popular shopping district, Oxford Street, or take a trip to the high-end hotspot shopping centre, Harrods. Foodies should head to famous Borough Market to stock up on amazing produce to enjoy in your apartment, or sample divine food from the many stalls inside this historic building. Borough Market is one of the largest and oldest food markets in the capital and has a long heritage – there’s been a market on the site dating back to the twelfth century!

Food & Drink
You will truly be spoiled for choice when it comes to food and drink, with so many varied and exciting restaurants in the immediate area. A great coffee shop just 2 minutes from your apartment is Harris + Hoole, serving seasonally sourced, single origin coffee. Within a couple of minutes’ walk of your apartment you’ll find a wide range of lunch and dinner options: Plants of Roselyn is the place to go for plant-based authentic Thai cuisine; Flat Iron London Bridge is an industrial-chic steak restaurant; Pizza Pilgrims is a pizzeria housed in a beautiful archway under London Bridge station, offering outside seating and creative toppings; and Santo Remedio is a Mexican restaurant offering a cool take on traditional street food in gorgeous, bright surrounds. For something special, head to one of the restaurants housed in the Shard, or try the sophisticated South African cuisine on offer at Vivat Bacchus.

Night Life
Again, being so centrally located means you have plenty of options for your evening. Bars abound in this part of town, each with their own unique twist on a night out. Try retro-styled Electric Shuffle for drinks and shuffleboard games under the arches of London Bridge station. At Katzenjammers, lederhosen-clad staff will serve you Bavarian beers at wooden benches while a live oompah band entertains the beer hall. On Holyrood Street, Nine Lives is an amazing snug neighbourhood gem of a cocktail bar, offering brilliant drinks and a great soundtrack in a Victorian basement. And there are, of course, plenty of traditional pubs and taverns – The George, a 17th-century coaching inn, is one of London’s oldest pubs and featured in Charles Dickens’ Little Dorrit. Or for a drink with riverside views, head to the beer garden at The Anchor – it’s the sole survivor of the river taverns of Shakespeare’s day, having been rebuilt after the great fire of London.

Nestling in the heart of Kensington, these beautifully appointed one-bedroom and studio apartments are perfect for both business and leisure guests.

Official property page — Things to do around High Street Kensington Serviced Apartments - Cheniston Gardens

Introduction
Cheniston Gardens is a popular residential road in Central London with easy access to the outstanding shopping and dining opportunities on offer around Kensington High Street. High Street Kensington tube station is three minutes' walk away with convenient onward travel to the key business hubs and tourism attractions around the capital. Just beyond Kensington High Street lies the beautiful Kensington Gardens, where you'll find the Serpentine Gallery and the iconic Royal Albert Hall at its fringe. The Design Museum is a 10-minute walk from our apartments, featuring exhibitions and displays focused on contemporary design; beyond it, you’ll find the landscaped delights of Holland Park.

Shopping
Round the corner from Viridian Apartments High Street Kensington, you'll find Kensington High Street, a major shopping scene running from Hammersmith straight through to Kensington Gardens. The street features a wide variety of brand name stores with cafés and restaurants conveniently sprinkled in amongst them. At its center the high street is intersected by Kensington Church Street which offers a wonderful selection of high end fashionable outlets. If you're looking for antiques, the District and Circle Line connects you to Notting Hill Gate and Portobello Road Market. Oxford Street, one of Europe's most popular shopping destinations can also be reached easily by bus or tube.

Food & Drink
There is a wonderfully eclectic range of eateries in the area, spanning Italian, French, Indian, British and American cuisines. On the corner of Cheniston Gardens you’ll find cosy traditional English tearoom, The Muffin Man Tea Shop, offering tea and coffee, cakes and pastries, plus selling loose tea. Or head to Café Nouvelle if you’re looking for a classic coffee shop. Maggie Jones’s, an 8-minute walk away, serves a hearty farmhouse-style British menu in a relaxed space decorated to look like a renovated barn – think beehives, buckets and wicker baskets. Como Garden(8-minute walk) serves Italian tapas in an upscale plant-filled space, while Dishoom(6-minute walk) is a popular spot for elevated Bombay comfort food and first-class drinks.

Night Life
On Kensington High Street, trendy High Spirit Cocktail Bar combines great drinks with a warm atmosphere while neighbourhood spot Amaro Bar offers fine drinks, finger foods and live music on select evenings. Perhaps you’d prefer a more relaxed evening? Try one of the many great pubs in the area. The Britannia is resplendent with wood-panelled walls, leather armchairs and a conservatory dining room – just 4 minutes’ walk from our apartments. The stylish Devonshire Arms(3 minutes’ walk) has a fabulous outside space in which to enjoy a summer evening, while The Builder’s Arms(11 minutes’ walk) is a relaxed spot for craft beers, fine wines and artisan spirits.

Official property page — Things to do around Canning Town Serviced Apartments

Introduction
This superbly located building is a short walk to all local amenities including coffee shops, restaurants and sports facilities. Canning Town station is a five-minute walk from your apartment, providing easy access across the city. If you’re looking for green spaces, Bow Creek & East India Dock Basin and Canning Town Recreation Ground are all popular, with the latter boasting tennis courts, a wildflower meadow, a climbing wall and the Cycle Speedway Club. Trinity Buoy Wharf, a riverside centre for arts and cultural activities, regularly hosts exhibitions and events. In nearby Canary Wharf you’ll find the Crossrail Place Roof Garden, offering a haven of calm and great views of the skyline; admire the exotic plants, wander down the hidden pathways or enjoy a show at the amphitheatre. While there, stop in at the Museum of London Docklands to learn more about how the docks have shaped London’s history. It’s a short train ride to Stratford, where the Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park offers world class culture, sport and iconic architecture – make sure to visit the ArcelorMittal Orbit, London's largest piece of public art, designed by Anish Kapoor.

Shopping
The Hallsville Quarter, six-minutes’ walk from your apartment, is home to a blend of high street and independent shops, cafes, bars, restaurants and leisure facilities; while Rathbone Market offers fresh produce, vibrant street food and fashion four days a week. The neighbourhood also benefits from being close to Stratford, with Westfield Stratford City shopping centre only two stops away on the train, providing a huge selection of high street shops and designer brands. In nearby Canary Wharf, Cabot Place is a goldmine of interesting stores and designer brands – check out Aesop for ethically sourced skincare and fragrance, Charbonnel et Walker for fine chocolates, and Crockett and Jones for high quality Goodyear-welted footwear with a 135-year heritage.

Food & Drink
There are plenty of coffee shops, restaurants, cafés and pop-up shops in the local area, offering a range of cuisines. Within easy walking distance of your apartment you’ll find Pepenero serving authentic Italian using locally sourced ingredients where possible, Petit Café London offering delicious Lebanese cuisine – and we love The Lockdown Room, where you’ll find everything from coffee and street food, to craft beer and live music. On Barking Road, visit 55Square Restaurant for West African food and delicious cocktails. Pie and mash is an East London classic – check out B.J.’s Pie & Mash, or Eastenders Pie & Mash in nearby East India Dock. Looking for something sweet? Take a six-minute walk to Brass Monkey Ice Cream, specialising in organic ice cream, homemade cakes and locally roasted coffee.

Night Life
Yapix Coffee & Wine House is a lovely spot to sample a curated list of Italian wines, sustainably sourced and rotating to compliment seasonal menus of Puglian cuisine. Or walk down to the beach at Royal Victoria Dock where you’ll find The Oiler Bar set on a boat with a beer garden and a snug seating area below deck - take in great views of the Royal Docks, and once a month it hosts an open-mic night (we’ve heard it’s great fun!). Canning Town is a short, 10-minute train ride from the eclectic mix of restaurants and bars in Canary Wharf. At Crossrail Place you can sip a cocktail while enjoying panoramic views of the city skyline at Pergola on the Wharf, or catch a movie at luxury cinema Everyman which has three screens and a bar inside.

Official property page — neighbourhood and apartment
Viridian Apartments Kensington is set within a beautiful Victorian townhouse, located in a quiet residential street in the heart of Kensington, a famously upscale neighbourhood with a wealth of destinations on its doorstep.
Inside, one- and two-bedroom apartments are available, some with sought after private outside space (please email stay@viridianapartments.com if outside space is important to you). Each apartment has been recently refurbished and tastefully decorated and is equipped with modern amenities and comfortable furnishings.
All apartments offer a fully fitted kitchen (including a dishwasher and a washer-dryer) a modern bathroom with shower, spacious and comfortable open plan living areas with free Wi-Fi, TV and double-glazed windows.
This luxury location is less than 10 minutes’ walk to Earl's Court and Gloucester Road underground stations and a pleasant walk to High Street Kensington.

Official property page — Things to do around Kensington Serviced Apartments - Lexham Gardens

Introduction
Lexham Gardens is a popular residential road lined with beautiful period properties. The location has easy access to the first-class shopping and dining opportunities on offer around Kensington High Street. Earl's Court and Gloucester Road tube stations are a few minutes' walk away with convenient onward travel to the key business hubs and tourism attractions around the capital. Some of the area’s best landmarks can be easily reached by public transport or even a leisurely stroll, including the Natural History Museum, Science Museum, V&A Museum, Royal Albert Hall and Kensington Gardens, so you are spoiled for choice when it comes to things to do. Two hidden gems to visit are Leighton House & Sambourne House, two neighbouring homes of Victorian artists which have now been turned into some of London’s most photogenic museums. And screen buffs should wander down Kynance Mews, which has appeared in several films including The Big Sleep, and in TV shows such as Netflix’s You.

Shopping
Kensington High Street, a major shopping scene running from Hammersmith straight through to Kensington Gardens, is within easy walking distance. A wide variety of brand name stores, cafés and restaurants are on hand as well as a selection of high-end fashionable outlets on Kensington Church Street. If you're looking for antiques, the District and Circle Line connects you to Notting Hill Gate and Portobello Road Market. Oxford Street, one of Europe's most popular shopping destinations can also be reached easily by bus or tube.

Food & Drink
Get your caffeine fix at cool Danish café Hjem; this snug community spot serves speciality coffee, pastries and bread, made using organic and locally-sourced ingredients. For lunch or dinner, you could try one of the nearby gastropubs. The Abingdon (10-minute walk) is a quaint art-deco spot that has been run by the Staples family since 1998 – head there for a modern British menu that celebrates the best of local, and a curated wine list to pair. Meanwhile, the stylish Devonshire Arms (5-minute walk) has a fabulous outside space in which to enjoy a summer evening meal and drink with friends or colleagues. French classics abound at Margaux (12-minute walk), a restaurant and wine bar in a stylish urban setting, while Dishoom (12-minute walk) is a popular spot for elevated Bombay comfort food and first-class drinks. And if you’re looking to use your fully-equipped apartment kitchen, a Sainsbury’s can be found just round the corner.

Night Life
Theatre fans might like to visit the Royal Court, only 13 minutes away from our apartments via the District line at Earl’s Court station; it’s Britain's leading national theatre company dedicated to showing work by innovative new writers. For concerts, the Royal Albert Hall is one of the capital’s most iconic venues and the place to see the BBC Proms each summer. Cadogan Hall, about 15 minutes away by tube, is a historic classical music venue in nearby Chelsea and is home of the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra – you’ll also find performances from jazz and folk musicians taking place here. For live music that is a little more laid back, Piano Kensington (13 minutes’ walk from our apartments) features an elongated bar and live piano music six nights a week, with jazz on Sundays, although you will need to book ahead. There are also plenty of pubs and bars in and around the area in which to enjoy an evening.

Our stylishly furnished apartments, located in the heart of Fitzrovia, are ideal for both business and leisure stays.
Charlotte Street is lined with galleries, restaurants and old-school pubs, with a wonderfully bustling atmosphere. The property also has easy access to the world-renowned shopping amenities of Oxford Street, Regent Street and New Bond Street, ensuring guests are perfectly positioned to make the most of the West End location.
This attractive period building offers high-quality two-bedroom apartments, boasting natural light and charm. Each serviced apartment has a fully-fitted kitchen with a full-sized fridge/freezer, a dishwasher, washer/dryer, hob, oven and microwave.
Complimentary Wi-Fi (and free wired Internet), toiletries, hairdryer, iron/ironing board and a Smart TV are available to all guests.
Sleek, modern bathrooms offer baths with showers overhead.
Comfortable bedrooms offer luxurious king / double beds and plenty of storage space for clothes and belongings.

Official property page — Things to do around Fitzrovia Serviced Apartments - Charlotte Street

Introduction
One of London's oldest neighbourhoods, Fitzrovia once housed many luminaries including author George Orwell and American Revolutionary Thomas Paine. One of London's most well-known parks, Fitzroy Square is named after the former owner of the property, Charles Fitzroy, Duke of Grafton, just like the rest of Fitzrovia. The area around Charlotte Street is home to new media, advertising, and architecture firms and is dotted with lodgings, art galleries, and bustling vintage taverns making it the perfect destination for young professionals and families alike.

Shopping
These serviced apartments are a short stroll from Oxford Street, where you’ll find plenty of high street brands, designer names and flagship stores to browse. Be sure to stop by the Liberty London department store – the Tudor-revival building itself is a treat, as are the luxury and premium stores inside (and of course, all things Liberty print!). In Soho, head to pedestrianised Carnaby to enjoy more than 100 stores including global names, British heritage labels, independent boutiques, one-off concepts, beauty emporiums, and bespoke jewellers. The cobbled streets of the Newburgh Quarter are where you’ll find cool independent stores selling everything from fashion to homeware and art. Need a breather? Kingly Court is Carnaby’s iconic three-story al-fresco food and dining destination with 25 restaurants to choose from.

Food & Drink
In just a few minutes’ walk from our apartments you’ll find a huge variety of cafés, pubs and restaurants. Just up Charlotte Street, Italia Uno is a beloved sandwich bar – get there early to avoid the queues! Or check out Shoop Soup for a globally-inspired menu with plenty of vegan and vegetarian options too. The Riding House Café is a great place for a delicious brunch or casual breakfast meeting, or try Lore of the Land where you’ll find seasonal pub classics and excellent pints. There are plenty of dinner options in the vicinity offering a vast array of cuisines. Argentinian food and wine is served in a lavishly designed restaurant at Gaucho, which also seeks to be as environmentally-friendly as possible. At Hakkasan Hanway you can sample mouth-watering Cantonese cuisine with a Michelin-star experience; or check out 28°-50° Oxford Circus for delicious European food in chic surrounds, and a curated wine list to pair.

Night Life
The proximity to London’s West End – it’s walkable in under 20 minutes – means theatre lovers can kick off the evening with a show. Head to the Dominion Theatre for musicals, catch Les Misérables at the Sondheim Theatre or check out comedy and cabaret at The Soho Theatre. Fancy a cocktail? There are plenty of options to choose from! Mr Fogg’s House of Botanicals is a feast for the eyes, with flora and fauna to match the botanical-inspired cocktails served at this Fitzrovia bar. At Bourne & Hollingsworth Bar, you can enjoy imaginative concoctions in quaint surroundings, with wall murals galore. If you like seated service, head to Goodge Street where you can sample innovative takes on classic drinks at the ‘secret’ underground bar Reverend J W Simpson.

Official property page — neighbourhood and apartment
These centrally located and contemporary one and two bedroom serviced apartments are housed in a traditional Victorian building.

The one bedroom apartment offers a spacious master bedroom featuring a double bed, in addition to another small bedroom / study.

All two bedroom apartments benefit from two bathrooms.

One apartment benefits from a patio, another from a balcony (please enquire stay@viridianapartments.com if outside space is important to you).

With solid wood parquet flooring, stunning kitchens with all the latest appliances and modern bathrooms, these apartments make for a very comfortable stay - whether staying for business or leisure.

Earl’s Court, close to South Kensington, is a very suitable location if you want to sit back and relax amongst the local London bars and restaurants.

You can also take the short tube journey into the bustling West End.

For football fans, Stamford Bridge lies down the road from the Earl’s Court apartment – the home of Chelsea FC.

Official property page — Things to do around Earl's Court Serviced Apartments - West Brompton - 25 Ongar Road

Introduction
Situated in Earl’s Court and close to South Kensington, these apartments are in a very convenient location from which to reach the City, West End and Heathrow.

Within easy walking distance are the restaurants and bars of Earl’s Court and South Kensington, or head to nearby Chelsea for the boutiques of Brompton Road and King’s Road and mix with celebrities at Bluebird or Bouji’s. This leafy suburb offers a real slice of London living and the perfect base for a business traveller seeking a work/life balance.

Shopping
Just two stops on the Overground will get you to Shepherd’s Bush, where you’ll find hundreds of big-name brands, designer stores and smaller boutiques at Westfield London. In nearby Chelsea, head to King’s Road where there are over 160 shops ranging from small boutiques and pop-ups to iconic department store Peter Jones. Claudie Pierlot is the place for Parisian-chic styles, while Flying Tiger houses hundreds of Scandi knick-knacks. And over at Farm Fetch, you can shop a carefully curated selection of foods and produce sourced from small-scale local producers across different regions in Italy.

Food & Drink
Earl's Court is also filled with many places to eat and relax. For a breakfast stop, POPS cafe is a great destination, from interesting teas and coffees to full breakfast fry-ups. Black Rabbit Cafe is a lovely spot for specialty coffee, smoothies, breakfasts and brunch. Just a few moment's walk from your serviced apartment is The Prince; featuring three restaurants playing host to some of London’s most exciting new chefs and a beautiful garden with a retractable roof where you can enjoy food and drink with friends. The Lillie Langtry, just opposite, is also a great choice for pub grub made with quality ingredients sourced from local suppliers. For dinner plans, Addie’s Thai is one of Earl's Court’s more popular restaurants. The menu consists of hearty dishes from Asia, with dishes ranging from noodles and rice to fish and crab.

Night Life
Head to Evans and Peel Detective Agency, a short 11-minute walk from your serviced apartment, if you fancy drinks with a side of vintage surroundings and a Prohibition-era vibe. This cool bar is an Earl's Court staple where you can enjoy clandestine cocktails based on famous detective cases, and American eats if you're feeling peckish. For a relaxed spot to meet with friends, try neighbourhood wine bar Vagabond where you can sample some of the 100+ wines available, alongside some tapas-style sharing plates or a charcuterie board. And if you’re in the mood for something lively, late-night cocktail bar Simmons in nearby Fulham offers a long happy hour, a beer pong table and retro games consoles to keep you occupied.

Official property page — Things to do around Earl's Court  Serviced Apartments - West Brompton - 6 Ongar Road

Introduction
Our serviced apartments on Ongar Road are situated a short walk from West Brompton station and in easy reach of the many attractions in Earl’s Court, Kensington and Chelsea, but there's plenty to enjoy in the local area too. This leafy suburb offers a taste of London living for those in town for leisure, while being the perfect base for a business traveller. The area is home to Stamford Bridge stadium, where the Chelsea Football Club plays – you can go behind-the-scenes with a tour. A cemetery might not be an obvious choice for an afternoon stroll, but Grade I listed Brompton Cemetery is actually a Royal Park! Explore historic monuments, enjoy tranquil greenery and learn the stories of the people interred in its beautiful landscape. Or perhaps head to urban winery London Cru, tucked down a side street two minutes from our apartments, where you can enjoy tastings, tours and regular events.

Shopping
West Brompton Crossing is a ‘pop-up high street’ just a moment or two from our serviced apartments, with a great collection of independent restaurants, shops, pop-ups and event spaces to explore. West Brompton is also well-located for the shopping delights of Fulham, Kensington, Earl’s Court and Knightsbridge. Just two stops on the Overground will get you to Shepherd’s Bush, where you’ll find hundreds of big-name brands, designer stores and smaller boutiques at Westfield London. In nearby Chelsea, head to King’s Road for a mile of retail heaven; cult fashion stores include Anthropologie, Bimba y Lola and ME+EM while The Furniture Cave, a beautiful building in and of itself, boasts three floors of antique treasures. And of course, don’t miss out on a visit to iconic Harrods in Knightsbridge – explore the beauty halls, find a perfect outfit or head to the fresh market hall for premium seasonal produce.

Food & Drink
You’ll immediately notice the jewel-toned exterior of The Hoarder on Lillie Road; inside you’ll find award-winning, world class coffee as well as pastries, nibbles and condiments to buy for later. For a heartier meal, a Michelin-starred lunch or dinner is a mere five minutes’ walk from our apartments at the Harwood Arms. Sustainability is a focus - the establishment proudly serves consciously-sourced British food, with a focus on game, using its rooftop vegetable garden for fresh and seasonal ingredients. Slightly further afield, The Fox and Pheasant has been serving English food and drinks since the 1840s; tucked away behind Stamford Bridge stadium, this charming tavern offers a country feel right in the heart of bustling West London. Enjoy homemade organic Mediterranean dishes at Jak’s King’s Road, head to La Pappardella for traditional Italian and amazing pizzas, or sample the tastiest borscht in London at Mriya Neo Bistro, which provides a modern twist on Ukrainian cuisine.

Night Life
The Finborough Theatre, a short 10-minute stroll from our apartments, is a multi-award-winning local gem offering a programme of stimulating and inclusive theatre. After an evening show head to the Troubadour, London's original and last remaining independent live music venue from the coffee-house era. The stage has been graced by music legends such as Jimi Hendrix, Bob Dylan, Joni Mitchell and Adele, and the venue still proudly hosts live music every night. For a perfect spot to meet with friends, head to neighbourhood wine bar Vagabond and sample some of the 100+ wines available, alongside some tapas-style sharing plates or a charcuterie board. And if you’re in the mood for something lively, late-night cocktail bar Simmons in nearby Fulham offers a long happy hour, a beer pong table and retro games consoles to keep you occupied.

Official property page — neighbourhood and apartment
This stunning collection of spacious one- and two-bedroom duplex apartments and mews houses sits in prime central Hammersmith and offers private outside space.

Newly built in 2023, Southerton Mews is a perfect home from home whether staying for business, relocating or leisure. The sought-after location is less than five minutes’ walk from Hammersmith underground station offering easy access around the capital. With an abundance of shops, bars, cafes, restaurants and theatres nearby, the amenities within walking distance could not be better.

Nestling at the end of a no-through road, the duplex apartments are within a highly attractive new-build property with the mews houses sitting behind through a private gated entrance. A pretty cobbled path lined with climbing foliage makes for a truly welcoming ambience.

Southerton Mews has been expertly interior designed with precision and flair. The contemporary furniture is sleek and sophisticated, chosen with comfort in mind. Open plan living areas with wooden flooring feature a large sofa with coffee table and smart TV. Custom-designed kitchen units come complete with high-spec, integrated appliances, including fridge/freezer, dishwasher, electric hob, oven and washer-dryer. There’s ample dining space with large tables and comfy padded dining chairs. Perfect for relaxing or entertaining.

Bedrooms are finished with carpeted flooring, ensuring they are well insulated. They come equipped with high-quality beds with top-range Silentnight mattresses. Built in wardrobes, cupboards and bedside cabinets offer plenty of storage space. Bathrooms are modern and pristine. All accommodation comes with a bath with shower over head and some also offer a second bathroom with walk-in shower.

With great practicality, all apartments with one bathroom also house a second guest restroom.

All apartments and mews houses have the benefit of private outside space with a terrace or balcony.

Sustainability credentials

The property is a gas-free development, including Air Source Heat Pumps and underfloor heating to maximise their efficiency, providing heating and hot water throughout.

A mechanical ventilation system with NOx filtration has been fitted which is designed to filter polluted air. The compact system uses combined particulate and gas filters to reduce levels of Nitrogen Dioxide and particulate matter to within target limits making the air safer to breathe.

The design of this property also incorporates the requirements of Sustainable Urban Drainage Systems (SUDS). This is a natural approach to managing drainage and works by slowing and holding back the water that runs off from a site, allowing natural processes to break down pollutants.

Recycling waste management is available on site.

Eco-friendly materials include FSC-certified timber, mattresses made from recycled marine plastic and toiletries packaged in bottles made from wheat straw and recycled plastics.

Following a stay there in the Spring of 2023, The Business Travel Magazine listed this property as one of the UK's best sustainable serviced apartments.

Official property page — Things to do around Hammersmith Serviced Apartments - Southerton Mews

Introduction
Our serviced apartments are found right in the heart of Hammersmith, with all the brilliant cultural attractions in easy walking distance. The Apollo, Hammersmith’s legendary performance venue, is ten minutes away, while an eclectic programme of theatre can be found at the Lyric just five minutes away. Riverside Studios used to be home to BBC Television’s iconic programmes, including Doctor Who in the 1960s; now you’ll find a premier independent cinema, theatre and restaurant on site. Amble down to Grade II* listed Hammersmith Bridge, where you’ll find trails winding along the River Thames – perfect for an afternoon stroll. It also boasts a great vantage point to view the annual Oxford and Cambridge Boat Races, as the bridge falls about halfway through the route. And with Hammersmith tube station a few moments’ walk from our serviced apartments, exploring the very best the capital has to offer is easy and efficient.

Shopping
Busy King Street is lined with plenty of well-known fashion brands as well as smaller independent shops. A couple of local gems that we like include Maison Samadi for luxury handmade chocolates and charity shop Traid for vintage threads – treasure seekers will delight in discovering a unique designer piece among the preloved fashion. King Street is also where you’ll find the Livat Shopping Centre; make sure to check out Atelier100 inside, which offers homeware, clothing and jewellery designed and produced by local creatives. By the tube station, there’s also the Broadway Shopping Centre, with over 20 retail stores to explore. Further afield, it’s a short 11-minute tube to Westfield in nearby Shepherd’s Bush, where you’ll find designer fashion, high-street brands, and quirky independent boutiques – a shopper’s dream.

Food & Drink
With the brilliant location of our serviced apartments, you have a world of cuisines in short walking distance. Excellent coffee, tempting pastries and healthy dishes are just five minutes away at family-friendly Daily Shot. Colourful bakery Patisserie Sainte Anne is a wonderful little spot for homemade breads and pastries, cakes, macarons and chocolates – it’s like a little bit of Paris in the heart of Hammersmith! Pop over to Lyric Square where you’ll find the Hammersmith Food Market on Thursdays and the World Food Market on Fridays. It’s a true melting pot of cuisines, with Filipino, Caribbean, Moroccan and Ghanaian hot food stalls, plus fresh produce. There are also plenty of restaurants nearby. At Patri you can enjoy Indian street food dishes that founder Puneet Wadhwani once ate as a child growing up near New Delhi train station. Often-recommended Mahdi brings fine Persian cuisine to Hammersmith, or pay a visit to The Gate for plant-based dishes enjoyed al fresco in the charming secret garden. Looking to make a meal in your fully-fitted apartment kitchen? Pick up organic, fairtrade produce at Bushwacker Wholefoods.

Night Life
If you like to enjoy a drink in a historic local, Hammersmith has plenty to choose from. Of course, infamous historic pub The Dove is a must – Ernest Hemingway, Graham Greene, Dylan Thomas and William Morris all visited the bar in their time. Admire the tiled exterior of The Salutation on King Street or visit Victorian pub The Hop Poles where you can enjoy a tipple on the roof terrace. After a show at the Lyric Theatre why not round off the evening with a casual drink at Brackenbury Wine Rooms? With 40 wines available by the glass, a wide terrace and plenty of seating inside too, it’s the perfect place to socialise over some top wines and tapas-style snacks – and it’s only a five-minute walk back to your apartment!

Official property page — neighbourhood and apartment
If you are looking for an apartment within walking distance to Wembley Stadium, look no further. These beautifully appointed one- and two- bedroom apartments are in a prime location less than 3 minutes’ walk to Wembley Stadium overland train station and less than 10 minutes’ walk to both Wembley Central and Wembley Park underground stations. An extensive transportation network for quick and convenient access to the rest of the capital.

The building boasts spacious apartments and plenty of natural light, making it a great choice for anyone looking for a bright and airy living space. The lounge area comes with a sofa and Smart TV, a perfect spot to unwind. You'll find open-plan, fully-integrated dining kitchens (complete with dishwashers and washer/dryers) as well as comfortable bedrooms and contemporary bathrooms. All the duplex apartments (1.5 bedroom units) come with a balcony, allowing you to enjoy private outside space with views of the surrounding area.

There is a handy elevator to all floors and off-road parking is available to book via our reservations team. Free Wi-Fi comes as standard.

The apartments are ideally located in one of London's most exciting neighbourhoods, close to the iconic Wembley Stadium, the popular London Designer Outlet centre and the London Arena which hosts major musical and sporting events. Wembley is a bustling and vibrant area, well-renowned for the great restaurants and nightlife options – you’ll have plenty to keep you entertained during your visit.

Official property page — Things to do around Wembley Stadium Serviced Apartments

Introduction
Our serviced apartments are perfectly placed in the heart of bustling Wembley. The iconic stadium, which plays host to major sporting and music events, is less than ten minutes’ walk away – and you might even spot the famous arch from our apartment balconies! The cultural hub of Wembley Park is a 15-minute walk away, offering an abundance of entertainment and shopping to enjoy as well as a free art trail with 22 incredible pieces of public art to view as you explore this vibrant area. While there, visit the Troubadour Wembley Park Theatre for world-class entertainment or head to BOXPARK for amazing street food, then try your hand at axe throwing, crazy golf, shuffleboard, table tennis, pool or table football. If you’re looking to enjoy the great outdoors, Fryent Country Park is an 11-minute drive with more than 100 hectares of rolling fields and small woods to explore. Transport links are excellent, giving you easy access to the capital: Wembley Stadium station, 3 minutes from our apartments, offers a train to Marylebone in 9 minutes while Paddington station is a 20 minute train from nearby Wembley Central station.

Shopping
At our Wembley Stadium serviced apartments you’re well-placed for two shopping centres less than 10 minutes’ walk away. On the High Street, Wembley Central Shopping Centre offers a mix of high street retailers, while at Wembley Park shopping enthusiasts can enjoy huge discounts on designer brands at London Designer Outlet. There is also a large food court inside as well as a cinema screening the latest blockbusters. If you’re staying in the area when the monthly Wembley Park Antiques Market is on, make sure to stop by for a curated selection of one-of-a-kind pieces, quirky antiques and vintage items; treasure seekers can find everything from fashion and accessories to artwork, homeware and books.

Food & Drink
BOXPARK is a hub of food stalls offering plenty of choice when it comes to cuisine: Argentinian steak, Caribbean classics, Malaysian and Filipino street food, Hawaiian poké bowls, sushi, fish and chips and more... there’s something for everyone to explore and enjoy! For excellent independent coffee, try Boki Coffee or head to Acai Verao for healthy breakfast bowls, smoothies and juices. At Bread Ahead the all-day menu serves everything from tempting doughnuts and French toast to stone-baked pizza and burgers. Pasta Remoli is the spot for fast and delicious Italian while Masalchi, from Michelin-starred chef Atul Kochhar, brings Indian street food to Wembley Park. By the stadium, Mezze Grill is a popular place to enjoy Turkish cuisine and sharing platters – it’s been lauded as the best Turkish food in London! Those with a sweet tooth should definitely check out Haute Dolci for beautiful desserts; while there, make sure you snap a photo of the indoor cherry tree and pastel-perfect interiors.

Night Life
In Wembley Park, you can enjoy an evening of comedy or theatre at the Troubadour before heading to British pub The White Horse, which has a lovely terrace for al fresco summer drinks. Its close proximity to the stadium means the pub draws a lively crowd on event days keen to enjoy the local ales, draught beer, lengthy wine list and pub food classics on offer. Las Iguanas, housed at London Designer Outlet, offers vibrant cocktails, a generous happy hour and a salsa soundtrack. As well as Latin twists on classic drinks, you can try a ‘carbon friendly cocktail’ - Las Iguanas will plant a tree in Latin America for every 10 sold. On the high road, just 4 minutes’ walk from our serviced apartments, The Liquor Station is a fun, popular place for drinks and also often hosts DJ nights on the weekend.

Official property page — neighbourhood and apartment
Nestled between the neighbourhoods of Kensal Rise, Ladbroke Grove, Portobello Road and Notting Hill, our two-bedroom apartments in North Kensington are the epitome of chic. The stylish interiors have been consciously designed to create a relaxed space, with floor to ceiling windows lending a bright, airy feel and plenty of natural light.

The apartments are beautifully appointed with parquet wooden floors, contemporary furniture, and zoned spaces so you can cook, dine, work and relax in comfort. Open-plan kitchens come equipped with everything you need, including a dishwasher, washer/dryer and oven; combined with comfortable bedrooms and stylish, modern bathrooms to make these apartments a true home away from home.

Some apartments also have a balcony, a perfect spot to unwind on summer evenings. The building also benefits from an elevator and complimentary Wi-Fi comes as standard.

The location is excellent whether staying for business or leisure. Three underground stations (Westbourne Park, Ladbroke Grove and Kensal Green) are all approximately 0.7 miles away from our apartments, offering a transport network across the capital via the Circle, Bakerloo and Hammersmith & City lines. Kensal Green also offers Overground trains towards London Euston and Watford Junction. The vibrant neighbourhoods of Notting Hill, Portobello Road and Ladbroke Grove offer an abundance of boutiques, independent stores, cafés, bars and restaurants to explore, as well as the iconic Portobello Road Market.

Please note that this property backs on to train tracks. Windows are double glazed.

Official property page — Things to do around North Kensington  Serviced Apartments - Portobello

Introduction
North Kensington is a well-connected area found between Kensal Rise, Ladbroke Grove, Portobello Road and Notting Hill. Popular with both families and professionals, there are plenty of independent eateries, pubs, bars and green spaces in the immediate area. Westbourne Park, Ladbroke Grove and Kensal Green underground stations are all 0.7 miles away from our apartments, offering a transport network across the capital via the Circle, Bakerloo and Hammersmith & City lines, making North Kensington a great location for corporate travellers. Kensal Green also offers Overground trains towards London Euston and Watford Junction. Iconic Portobello Road Market is 0.8 miles away (around 16 minutes’ walk), lined with shops, stalls, bars and restaurants. The Grand Union Canal path is five minutes’ from our apartments; you can follow the Paddington Arm all the way to picturesque Little Venice, or simply enjoy a short stroll with a coffee on sunnier days.

Shopping
Treasure seekers should head to one of London’s best markets, Portobello Road, to explore the plethora of stalls selling antiques, bric-a-brac, fashion and more. Although the market is open every day of the week, Saturdays see the most vendors (and visitors), making for a vibrant shopping experience! Kensal Rise’s chic Chamberlayne Road is easily reached by foot in around 13 minutes, where you’ll find plenty of boutique fashion, homeware and gifting stores – check out Verandah for unique household items and presents. And Westfield London, reachable in 18 minutes by public transport, offers more than 350 retailers spanning big-name brands, fashion, accessories, beauty and homeware.

Food & Drink
Start your day with a specialty coffee and baked goods at Double Shot, a short walk from our apartments. The eatery also has fresh sandwiches and brunch options. Family-run café Panella, seven minutes’ walk away, is a beloved local restaurant bringing a rotating menu of Sicilian cuisine to North Kensington, with options for lunch and dinner. While there, be sure to check out Grade II* listed Trellick Tower, an icon of Brutalist architecture (although it certainly splits opinion!). Neighbourhood pub Parlour (8 mins walk) is a great place for an all-day menu of contemporary British food and craft beers, with seasonal dishes alongside the pub classics we all know and love. For a fancier dinner, LAYLOW restaurant is known for its celebrity clientele, deluxe interiors and modern European fare. To stock your apartment kitchen with organic, sustainable produce, try Golborne Deli (9 min walk) which sells everything from breakfast pastries and hearty salads to charcuterie and fine wine, all sourced from independent producers.

Night Life
Start your evening with a show at the Playground Theatre, around 10 minutes from our apartments by public transport. Housed in a former bus depot, this venue offers a programme of drama, musical theatre, comedy, festivals and performing art – including critically acclaimed and award-winning performances. In nearby Kensal Rise you’ll find London’s only social enterprise cinema, the Lexi, which is run by volunteers and shows everything from mainstream films to live opera, with proceeds going to charity. A tucked-away gem of a pub which is perfect for curated cocktails and great beer is The Eagle, a six-minute walk from our apartments – the interiors are gloriously colourful and the service warm. Towards Portobello Road, there are plenty of quirky bars in which to enjoy a drink. Kitschy interiors and concoctions with a Tiki twist are found at award-winning Trailer Happiness, while the Rococo-style bar at Beach Blanket Babylon, housed in a Georgian townhouse, offers a refined cocktail menu.
